artigo.texto: ProLogium and Rimac Technology Advance Next-Generation EV Battery Development Paris, France, October 12, 2026 – ProLogium today announced progress in its collaboration with Rimac Technology on next-generation electric vehicle battery pack development. The companies signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in September 2025 to develop a next-generation battery platform and have completed a battery pack concept mockup, which will be displayed at the 2026 Paris Motor Show. The next phase will focus on developing a functional battery segment to establish a basis for testing the thermal management and cell-integration concepts and support battery pack applications in the battery electric vehicle (BEV) market. The collaboration combines ProLogium’s next-generation cell technology with Rimac Technology’s battery system development expertise, focusing on a pouch cell-to-pack architecture. Through a staged development path from concept mockup to functional battery segment, full-scale functional battery pack and in-vehicle testing, the companies will progressively evaluate cell and system integration approaches, connecting next-generation cell technology with automotive product development. From Concept Mockup to Functional Hardware Bringing cell technology into automotive applications requires more than cell-level performance. It also involves addressing thermal management, cell integration and battery pack architecture at the system level. With battery pack integration at its core, the collaboration brings together cell technology and systems engineering to examine the design requirements for next-generation batteries in automotive applications. The completed concept mockup is an initial milestone in this development process. The ongoing development will move the project from a conceptual representation toward functional hardware, using a battery segment as the platform for subsequent testing. This work will assess the feasibility of thermal management and cell-integration concepts and inform full-scale battery pack development. By developing a battery segment before expanding to a full-scale system, the companies will gather test results and design feedback at each stage to assess whether the integration approach can meet automotive battery-systems requirements. Vincent Yang, Founder and CEO of ProLogium, said: Since jointly announcing our collaboration with Rimac Technology at IAA in 2025, both teams have continued to advance the project, translating our shared technical vision into concrete engineering development work. ”What we are presenting at the Paris Motor Show is the baseline of that collaboration. Building on the completed concept mockup and the functional segments currently in development, we are preparing to move into the development and production of a functional battery progressing toward a full-scale battery pack and subsequent vehicle integration validation. Bringing next-generation batteries to the automotive market requires more than cell technology. It also takes the engineering expertise to integrate those cells into a battery pack with optimized architecture and thermal management. We look forward to combining our technical strengths through hardware development and testing to address the engineering challenges of automotive integration and translate the value of next-generation cell technology into solutions that can be adopted in vehicles.” Daniel Kišić, Principal Product Architect of Rimac Technology said: Rimac Technology is developing a scalable cell-to-pack integration technology for solid-state pouch cells, designed to meet and exceed the requirements the automotive industry is expected to set over the coming decade. ”A wide range of integration solutions is currently being evaluated and tested in parallel on functional battery segments, covering thermal management, swelling management, cell integration and system-level design. Some of these solutions are oriented towards maximum energy density and reduced space and weight, while others are oriented towards delivering performance. The work starts from vehicle-level requirements and aims to improve every aspect of the battery design by reducing complexity, combining functions and reducing weight. It does so with cost in mind, while still delivering state-of-the-art charging times and power output. Once validated at vehicle level, the solution is expected to deliver significant weight savings, improving driving efficiency and extending range. OEMs could then choose between more energy on board at the same weight, a smaller and lighter battery for the same range, or any combination in between.” A Clear Pathway to Full-Scale Battery Packs and In-Vehicle Testing According to Rimac Technology’s current development roadmap, the functional battery segment currently in development is planned for display at CES 2027, with the full-scale functional battery pack identified as a development milestone for the second half of 2027. Subsequent targets include in-vehicle and public-road testing in the second half of 2028.These stages will progressively expand the scope of validation, from assessing integration concepts in a functional battery segment to a full-scale battery pack, followed by vehicle installation and road testing to evaluate system performance in an automotive environment. At the Paris Motor Show, the companies will present the concept mockup stage of the collaboration and outline the next steps in functional hardware development and integration validation. By combining cell technology with battery systems engineering, ProLogium and Rimac Technology will continue to advance next-generation battery integration technology development from concept design toward automotive applications. artigo.texto: On Wednesday afternoon, Jamie Robins strolled up to the entrance of Google’s UK headquarters in Kings Cross, London. He brandished a letter containing details of a petition signed by almost 55,000 people, calling for Google to abandon plans to build a large new data center in Thurrock, 15 miles to the east of London. Robins works for wildlife conservation trust Buglife, part of an unlikely alliance of special-interest groups trying to block the Thurrock development. Buglife and local wildlife groups fear for an endangered plant, rare bumblebee, and other invertebrates whose habitat they say will be destroyed. Nonprofit Foxglove says the data center will emit too much pollution. The Thurrock Hammers motorcycle club wants to return to racing on the site. Members of the various groups joined Robins outside Google’s office last Wednesday, holding placards demanding the company “search elsewhere” for somewhere to put its facility. Across the UK, companies like Google are preparing to build industrial-scale data centers, part of a scramble to meet the swelling demand for the compute needed to run artificial intelligence models and other digital services. The UK government is eager to encourage them, hoping to capture a share of the hundreds of billions of dollars flowing into the AI industry and minimize the country’s dependence on foreign partners for compute. But like in the US, people living near to the proposed developments are making their objections known and trying to gum up the works. Google says its plans for the Thurrock site prioritize biodiversity and the reduction of emissions. “We share the concerns that Buglife and others have—and their expectation that this site should be developed sustainably,” Adam Elman, director of sustainability EMEA at Google, tells WIRED. But the situation in Thurrock underscores the level and breadth of resistance that data center developers face as the public mood towards them appears to sour. Though small, the demonstration outside Google was one of a number of anti-data center protests that took place across Europe last week. In Amsterdam, protesters scaled a crane at a Microsoft data center site and unfurled a “fuck AI” banner. “There’s local campaign groups against data centers popping up every week,” says Robins. “People are angry about data centers turning up in their back gardens. They’re angry about data centers flouting local opinion—and about the impact it has on wildlife.” The Thurrock site is located next to a fuel stop, where an arterial road meets the highway that encircles London. On the plot, the remnants of Arena Essex, a disused motorcycle racing stadium, border grassland scribbled with old footpaths, and a lake. Google acquired the site through a subsidiary in 2023. In May last year, it applied for permission to build a data center campus there. When locals caught wind, they coordinated with national wildlife and environmental groups and began to kick up a fuss. Of the 1,000 responses submitted by members of the public to the planning authority, only one supported the project. (Thurrock Council says that many of the responses were submitted by people living outside the local area.) The protest group argues that Google’s proposal fails to properly account for the negative effects of the data center development: the loss of the raceway sporting facility, the destruction of habitat for rare flora and fauna, and the up to 570,000 tonnes of emissions it could produce each year—which Foxglove claims cannot be accommodated under the UK government’s carbon budget. “We’re an outlier. We object on different grounds. I think that’s why I think we’re quite useful to the whole campaign,” says Mark Sexton, director at the Thurrock Hammers motorcycle club. “The unlikely alliance has got some attention.” Google says the objections are grounded in misconceptions about its plans. The company claims it will achieve a net gain in biodiversity by retaining habitat and transplanting endangered plants to another location; and that it will offset the emissions by financing new sources of renewable energy generation, with a view to becoming carbon-neutral by 2030. Google argues that razing the motorcycle stadium will not result in the loss of an invaluable community facility because the track has already been out of use for a number of years. “We want to be good neighbors,” says Elman. “We recognize the ecological value of these sites. Our goal is to minimize the impact as much as possible.” Unconvinced by Google’s reassurances, the protesters intend to continue to fight the development—one small act of protest at a time. “Do I think we’ve got much hope? Not right now,” says Rob Pownall, founder of nonprofit Protect The Wild, who attended Wednesday’s demonstration. “But this is another chip off that massive ice block.” There are some signs the grassroots anti-data center movement is starting to win concessions. In the US, some states have instituted permitting freezes and data center moratoria, and pro-data center candidates were roundly crushed in this week’s midterm elections. In the UK, Foxglove recently succeeded in a legal challenge that forced the government to withdraw planning permission for a data center to the west of London. Thurrock Council tells WIRED it expects to rule on Google’s initial planning application early next year. After that, the company will need to come up with a more granular plan for developing the site, which will be subject to another lengthy vetting process. The protesters say they intend to make life hard for Google at every step. “These planning campaigns can go on for years,” says Robins. “It’s a war of attrition.”

artigo.texto: A chinesa Trina Storage avalia instalar uma fábrica de baterias no Brasil, mas só deve decidir depois de conhecer o tamanho do mercado aberto pelos primeiros leilões de armazenamento de energia do país, marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro. Em entrevista ao Canal Solar, a líder de Vendas da empresa para a América do Sul, Mariana Goudel, disse que a companhia já apresentou cotações para projetos que somam mais de 50 GWh de capacidade. O número reúne negociações em diferentes estágios, e não contratos fechados. «Tem um plano em andamento, sim, da Trina, onde a gente quer trazer uma fábrica nos próximos anos», afirmou a executiva, sem informar prazo nem valor de investimento. Segundo ela, apressar a fábrica para atender à primeira contratação poderia comprometer a execução e a qualidade dos equipamentos. Conteúdo local no primeiro leilão Os editais foram aprovados na semana passada pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). O leilão de 2 de dezembro exige conteúdo nacional, e o de 4 de dezembro é de ampla concorrência. Para o primeiro, a Trina pretende combinar equipamentos importados com componentes feitos no Brasil: a parte de corrente alternada, ligada à conversão de energia, terá produção local, enquanto a de corrente contínua será importada. Os sistemas oferecidos têm duração de quatro horas. A empresa também busca o credenciamento no BNDES para acessar linhas de financiamento, incluindo o Fundo Clima, que a executiva compara ao papel que o banco teve na expansão das cadeias eólica e solar. Entre os potenciais compradores estão geradoras, transmissoras, fundos de investimento e grupos estrangeiros. Ambição de metade do mercado Não é a primeira vez que a Trina mostra apetite pelo leilão. Em agosto, durante a feira Intersolar South America, Goudel disse à pv magazine Brasil que o objetivo da empresa era «levar 50% do leilão», com a plataforma Elementa 3, e citou uma carteira de mais de 50 clientes no país, com mais de 100 GWh em projetos em discussão. A expectativa do setor é que os leilões de dezembro inaugurem uma nova fase para o armazenamento no Brasil, hoje puxado por aplicações em comércio, indústria e áreas remotas. A Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento (Absae) projetava, na mesma feira, demanda de 4 a 5 GW nos certames. Para cumprir as exigências de nacionalização, a JA ESS também estuda parceiros locais, a CATL reforçou a parceria com a Moura e a Jinko ESS assinou memorando com a UCB.

artigo.texto: What to know: - Romulus City Council unanimously passed a 180-day data center moratorium. - Romulus Mayor Robert McCraight said the city currently has no data centers and has not received any data center proposals, but the moratorium will allow the Romulus Planning Commission to consider regulations. - The moratorium was amended to apply to all data centers. ROMULUS, Mich. — Romulus City Council voted unanimously to impose a 180-day moratorium on data center proposals while the city studies how to regulate the facilities. The moratorium takes effect immediately. It was initially proposed for data centers with an electrical demand of at least one gigawatt, but council members amended it to apply to all data centers. The resolution directs the Romulus Planning Commission to study how to measure data centers’ electrical demand and environmental impacts and consider appropriate zoning regulations. Mayor Robert McCraight said the pause will give officials time to develop an ordinance. “It’ll allow a little bit of time to draft an ordinance. It’ll give us some time to pull in some information, pull in some third parties, and give us expert opinions and not just pass legislation, good legislation,” McCraight said. McCraight said Romulus currently has no data centers and has not received any proposals. Some residents called for a complete ban. Resident Kelly Babowicz said a moratorium was not enough. “A moratorium on data centers is not sufficient for our city. Instead, we need to push for a complete ban on these facilities,” Babowicz said. Councilwoman Kathleen Abdo and Councilman William Wadsworth also suggested looking into an outright ban. McCraight said the city should consider whether smaller data centers could support local industry, including Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport. “There may be some need for data centers on a smaller level to support industry,” McCraight said. “DTW may need a data center to support their industries. So we don’t know. We need to look at all those facets before we pass legislation.”

artigo.texto: Next week, much of the industry will gather in Las Vegas for RE+ to talk about what gets built next. It’s an important conversation, but I’d encourage asset owners to bring a second question with them: what more can we get from what’s already been built? This question matters more than ever as electricity demand climbs and customers feel it on their monthly bill. EIA expects consumption to grow another 3.1% in 2027, driven largely by data centers and other commercial loads, while residential customers will pay nearly 5% more for power this year. The industry is working hard to add capacity, but getting it built takes time. According to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and GridTracker, the median project built in 2025 spent more than five years moving from interconnection request to commercial operation and only 13% of the capacity that requested interconnection between 2000 and 2020 had come online by the end of 2025. New generation is essential, but the fleet already operating is an opportunity we can’t afford to pass up. With nearly 52 gigawatts (GW) of utility-scale battery storage operating in the U.S. as of mid-2026, the installed base is too large to overlook and performance across it varies widely. When a battery energy storage system (BESS) falls short, the instinct is often to blame the battery and reach for augmentation or replacement, but in many cases the bottleneck is the controls, software and integration around it. Operating assets are under more pressure Higher prices should raise the value of delivering power when and where the grid needs it, yet revenues for many operating assets are moving in the other direction. In ERCOT, the average battery earned 84% less in 2025 than at its 2023 peak, as more storage competed for the same services. With incentive economics shifting too, asset managers face real pressure to get more from existing assets. At the same time, utilities are leaning on storage for grid stability. As more gas units face revenue pressure and retirement, the grid loses the spinning mass that provides inertia in the first moments of a disturbance. Grid-forming inverters can replace that inertia, often by upgrading existing storage rather than building new. Providing that support, alongside peak shaving, load shifting and voltage and frequency regulation, takes controls that respond faster than many legacy SCADA and EMS platforms were built to handle. Compliance requirements are moving just as quickly, with FERC Order No. 901 directing NERC to develop new reliability standards for inverter-based resources, including batteries, through 2030. Many plants operating today were designed before those requirements existed, increasing the importance of controls that can evolve as grid codes change. The same logic also applies to solar and wind plants. Once control functions are proven in the field they can easily be applied to other assets across the whole market. The battery isn’t always the bottleneck A recent Gridmatic study of 30 California batteries shows what’s at stake, with fleetwide availability averaging just under 80% and execution and bidding strategy driving a wide gap between top and bottom performers. Had every asset matched the leader, the group would have earned an estimated $98 million more over two years. The lesson isn't that every performance gap can be solved with software. It's that owners shouldn't assume the battery itself is the limiting factor. Before committing additional capital, owners should examine the full system: controls, software, market strategy, integration and plant-level coordination alongside battery health and hardware performance. Think about the smartphone in your pocket. Its hardware may be several years old, but software updates can improve how it performs and add capabilities that weren’t available when you bought it. Storage assets aren't so different: the physical equipment may still have years of useful life, while the controls and software around it can evolve to meet new market and grid requirements. A modern energy management and plant control platform layered onto existing assets can help owners: - Respond faster and more precisely to grid signals and market opportunities - Meet new grid code requirements through software rather than hardware - Expand operational flexibility and support additional value streams - Maximize usable energy through balancing and intelligent power allocation - Extend the competitive life of existing assets A controls retrofit in practice We saw this firsthand in the U.K., where our team, then part of Wärtsilä, worked with Zenobē to retrofit an existing 100 MW/100 MWh battery site with a new GEMS power plant controller. The upgrade took over energy management, secured grid compliance and added stateful grid-code functions such as de-load, along with control for multiple tenants sharing one point of interconnection. The batteries stayed in place, but the site gained new capabilities and is better prepared for future requirements. That same approach translates to U.S. markets, where interconnection rules and local regulations are evolving quickly. New deployments will remain critical, but the next wave of value may come from making today’s fleet work harder. As the industry gathers at RE+, owners should ask not just what they need to build next, but what more the assets already on the grid could deliver. Before replacing hardware or adding capacity, diagnose the whole plant. The constraint may not be the battery cells.

artigo.texto: FIRST ON FOX: A new analysis from a conservative AI safety group found that deep-red counties with large data centers or proposed projects shifted further toward Democrats in last week's midterm elections than comparable counties without such projects. Humans First’s analysis, obtained by Fox News Digital, examined public election returns and data-center project records in 1,540 counties across 16 states. The memo used several comparisons to measure what the group describes as a "data center penalty." Across all counties examined, those hosting large data centers shifted an additional 2.2 percentage points toward Democrats compared with non-host counties in the same states. The pattern appeared in 14 of the 16 states and 25 of the 27 governor and Senate races examined. Restricting the analysis to deep-red counties — those President Donald Trump won by at least 20 points in 2024 — produced a 2.1-point raw gap between counties hosting large data centers and comparable counties without projects. Among deep-red counties with projects still in the proposal stage, the gap was 1.1 percentage points after accounting for past voting patterns, rural or urban status, population size, racial and ethnic makeup and recent voting trends. TEA PARTY FOUNDER LAUNCHES NATIONWIDE 'DATA CENTER REVOLT' AGAINST AI DATA CENTER EXPANSION The group identified 114 proposed large data center projects across 92 deep-red counties, potentially setting up more local fights. The memo found that Republican vote totals fell an additional 1.1% in deep-red host counties compared with comparable counties without large data centers, while Democratic vote totals showed no significant change. The memo cautioned that its findings show an association rather than proof that data centers caused voters to change their behavior. County-level results also cannot determine whether Republicans switched their votes or simply stayed home. "Our analysis looked at how counties with data centers voted and how those counties moved to the left," Humans First Chairwoman Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital. "I think this happened for the reason I’ve been warning conservatives and Republicans about for some time: People engage politically when issues affect them personally. There’s nothing more personal than your pocketbook, your health care, your kids and family, your home and your community. A data center involves all of those things, which is why I believe these counties moved away from Republicans," she continued. Humans First’s September "Data Center Revolt" bus tour made 35 stops in 27 states, including 14 stops in the states covered by the analysis. Nine of those stops were in deep-red counties, all of which hosted a large data center project. Those nine counties shifted 2.2 points further toward Democrats after the analysis accounted for its controls, compared with a 0.75-point shift among deep-red host counties overall. The group said those same nine counties showed no comparable gap from 2020 to 2024. The findings do not establish whether the group's visits influenced voting behavior or whether those counties already had stronger opposition to data center development. Separately, voters favored restrictions on data center development or rejected measures supporting such projects in 46 of 47 local data center ballot measures in 2026, according to Ballotpedia. The measures included different types of proposals, including restrictions on development and advisory questions. Kremer said this is a local control issue, stressing that Republicans should focus on protecting property rights and ensuring people have control over how things affect their lives. "Whether you’re talking about AI technology or the infrastructure needed to build AI data centers, the American people have not had a seat at the table," Kremer said. "They haven’t had a say in how the technology affects them or how the data center buildout affects their communities. In many places across the country, developers and companies have gone in and cut deals behind closed doors, under a cloak of darkness, using nondisclosure agreements and shell companies. By the time people in the community find out about the project, it’s too late to stop it." "These projects affect the quality of life and how much money people have. They can increase the cost of electricity and water, while tax abatements are given to trillion-dollar companies — some of the wealthiest companies in the world. That is money coming out of the pockets of the American people," she continued. Kremer added, "When you talk about Iran and gas prices, tariffs and now the AI data center buildout, all of these costs are coming out of people’s pockets. That’s when people engage politically, and I think that’s what we saw last Tuesday." The concerns come amid a broader debate over how data centers should pay for the electricity and grid infrastructure they require. The Energy Department estimates data centers used 4.7% of U.S. electricity in 2024 and, in its reference case, could account for 11.8% by 2030. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has directed regional grid operators to address safeguards against shifting the costs of serving large electricity users onto other customers. Those developments do not establish that data centers caused higher household rates in the counties examined by Humans First. Tax incentives also vary by state. The National Conference of State Legislatures reported that at least 38 states offer incentives specifically for data centers, including equipment-tax exemptions and, in some states, exemptions involving electricity or property taxes. The Data Center Coalition, an industry trade group, says such incentives are similar to those offered to other capital-intensive industries and argues that data centers generate jobs, investment and tax revenue. Humans First does not support a nationwide or statewide moratorium on data centers, but Kremer said individual communities should be free to approve

artigo.texto: Resumo - Governo federal destina R$ 46,3 milhões ao desenvolvimento da plataforma Prisma - Projeto usa inteligência artificial para distribuir dados entre mini data centers - Finep administra os recursos; o CPQD fica responsável pela execução do convênio - Prazo de execução previsto é de 36 meses após a assinatura do acordo - Expectativa é reduzir gastos de energia e aumentar a proteção de dados estratégicos Ao Prisma, plataforma criada para administrar e repartir informações entre mini data centers espalhados pelo território nacional, a União aplicará R$ 46,3 milhões. O Ministério das Comunicações divulgou os detalhes nesta segunda-feira (9). Para definir onde e de que maneira os dados serão processados, a tecnologia se apoiará em inteligência artificial. Na prática, o sistema identifica o melhor destino para cada conjunto de dados e distribui de forma automática os recursos computacionais entre as diferentes infraestruturas. Com isso, o Executivo projeta queda nos gastos com energia e nos custos operacionais, além de acesso mais rápido às informações e maior proteção dos dados considerados estratégicos. Quem administra e executa o projeto Caberá à Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep) administrar os recursos, enquanto o Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD) se encarregará da execução. Assim, a partir da data em que as duas instituições assinarem o convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação, começa a contar o prazo definido, de 36 meses. Aposta em soberania digital Por fim, o tratamento de dados no país ganhará mais autonomia e soberania com a medida, na avaliação de Frederico Filho, ministro das Comunicações. Em nota, ele declarou: ‘Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior’.

artigo.texto: Estimated read time: 5-6 minutes - A Salem forum debated data centers' impact on Utah County communities and environment. - Volition's CEO defended its data center project amid concerns over pollution and resources. - Grassroots group Speak Up Utah seeks 7,000 signatures for a referendum on data center policies. SALEM, Utah County — A packed room at the Salem Community Center on Monday night heard from a panel of policymakers, technology leaders, conservation advocates and data center developers as Utahns wrestle with a growing question: Can data centers be developed responsibly? The discussion focused on transparency, community involvement and accountability as large-scale data center projects continue to move forward across despite mounting public concerns. Kieren McCord, civil and construction engineering professor at Brigham Young University, said communities should understand the various technologies available when evaluating proposed projects. "There's a lot of nuance in the types of mechanical cooling systems that you can use; there's a lot of nuance in the types of power generation, and those decisions are often made early on in the process," McCord said. "Knowing the options in each of those categories makes you able to ask for things, because maybe, maybe you just think 'No data center whatsoever.' But maybe you think, 'Yes, under the right conditions.'" One project at the center of the discussion was Volition, a data center development initially proposed near the mouth of Spanish Fork Canyon. The project is now planned for a site across I-15. Volition CEO Jeff Chavez said the new location is farther from existing homes. He said there are no plans for future residential development nearby. Chavez defended the project against concerns about pollution and resource consumption, arguing that Volition's model differs from many traditional data centers. "We have no electricity from the grid, no wasted water (and) a really strong economic return to the community," Chavez said. "We have no request for incentives. We meet all air emissions requirements." Grow the Flow executive director Ben Abbott said it should be required that all data centers are built with clean energy. "We can't sacrifice our air quality," Abbott said. "It used to be when the wind blew, that's when the inversion would clear out. Now, when the wind blows, we get pollution from Great Salt Lake because there are 1,200 square miles of exposed lakebed. So we also have to make sure that we aren't moving backwards when it comes to water conservation and security." Chavez also said data center operators should do more to reduce the visual impact of their facilities and make commitments to local communities. "Companies like ours can also volunteer and say, 'Here's our commitment,'" Chavez said. "'We will not work with nefarious companies. We do not work with surveillance, we do not work with the Department of War (and) we do not work with the Chinese.'" Members of the grassroots organization Speak Up Utah attended the event and said they are leading an effort to overturn Spanish Fork's recently approved data center ordinance through a referendum. The group has raised concerns about public input, air quality impacts and data privacy, among other issues. Chavez said Volition does not currently have a response to the referendum effort, adding that city leaders were well informed throughout the approval process and that many concerns had been addressed. "We really don't have a response to the referendum, because I think everything we did in the city, open hearings, the open houses that brought in several hundred people (and) website that details all of this site, we feel like the city is pretty well informed," he said. Carol-Lyn Jardine with grassroots organization Conserve Utah Valley said one of the main goals of the forum was informing residents about key issues with data centers before the Utah County Commission votes on a new policy. A previous planning commission meeting received a lot of attention after a physical altercation between an audience member and law enforcement. "While we're considering what the impacts are on people, on the environment, on the land (and) on water, and if we don't invite all voices to the table to have those kinds of conversations, we find that the rhetoric just gets dialed up on both sides," Jardine said. "When we can bring people together and have real dialogue where folks get to ask their hard questions and people who are looking at these projects get to hear the real concerns of residents, we can find more positive outcomes." Silicon Slopes CEO Clint Betts argued that industry and political leaders have not adequately explained the benefits data centers bring to Utah communities. "I can tell you who benefits from having a data center in your community: Elon Musk, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and the Department of War," Betts said. "Why do we need them?" Chavez countered that data centers support many technologies people use every day, from streaming services and videoconferencing platforms to emerging artificial intelligence tools. "There is an infinite number of systems that we rely on today because of data processing through a computer in a data center," Chavez said. "There's a lot of things that superintelligence and high-density computing is doing that is changing. Medicine is changing. Industry is making things much more efficient." Speak Up Utah organizers said they are seeking roughly 7,000 signatures to qualify their referendum effort. The group is hosting informational and signature-gathering events at the Spanish Fork Public Library.

artigo.texto: Os desafios dos Sistemas de Armazenamento Hidráulico no Brasil Os SAH são empreendimentos intensivos em capital e de prazo de maturação Atualizado O Setor Elétrico Brasileiro (SEB) atravessa um período sensível de mudanças estruturais, marcada pela expansão acelerada das fontes renováveis variáveis e da geração distribuída. Segundo o Balanço Energético Nacional (EPE, 2025) as fontes renováveis responderam por 86,8% da geração elétrica, enquanto eólica e solar alcançaram 26,4% do total. A capacidade instalada de energia eólica chegou a 34,7 GW e a fotovoltaica a 64,8 GW, dos quais a micro e minigeração distribuída correspondeu por 45 GW com 7,2 milhões de unidades consumidoras. Essa transição energética altera a composição de energias renováveis, mas aumenta a necessidade de deslocar a geração de outras fontes ao longo do dia, exigindo, cada vez mais potência e flexibilidade para manter o equilíbrio entre demanda e oferta. Nesse contexto de transição, a expansão do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) não pode adicionar apenas energia e potência, mas precisa ter flexibilidade para deslocar excedentes de energia no tempo. Assim, o Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) projeta um aumento dos cortes de geração por razões energéticas, ou seja, excesso de oferta, à medida que a expansão renovável e dos recursos energéticos distribuídos cresce mais rapidamente do que a demanda diurna. Armazenamento, potência e flexibilidade passam a ser atributos centrais e estratégicos para a expansão do SIN. A promulgação da Lei nº 15.269/2025 e as das regulamentações associadas ganham relevância para a superação dos problemas, através da construção de um arcabouço regulatório que reconhece o armazenamento no planejamento, estabelece regras de outorga, diferencia os Sistemas de Armazenamento Hidráulico (SAH) e orienta seus mecanismos competitivos de contratação. O desafio agora é transformar essas diretrizes investimentos. Os SAH podem efetivamente contribuir para integração das fontes solar e eólica, redução de restrições de geração, atendimento à ponta, resiliência energética, serviços ancilares, flexibilização e eventual postergação de investimentos em transmissão. Seu principal atributo é deslocar a geração de energia no tempo, já que consomem energia para bombeamento quando a eletricidade é abundante e ajudam a produzir energia quando é mais necessária. Em relação às baterias, os SAH apresentam vantagens quando são necessários grandes volumes de energia e períodos de armazenamento mais longos. As tecnologias tendem, portanto, a ser complementares: as baterias podem atender as necessidades de curta duração e resposta rápida, enquanto os SAH podem realizar ciclos diários prolongados e deslocamentos de maior duração (semanais, mensais ou sazonais). A evolução do planejamento ilustra essa mudança de escala. No Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia (PDE) de 2034 foi estimada 400 MW, já no PDE 2035, a necessidade chegou a aproximadamente 7 GW e, no PDE 2036, a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) passou a distinguir o armazenamento de curta e de longa duração. A Lei nº 15.269/2025 estabeleceu a sua base institucional ao reconhecer o armazenamento como atividade regulável, determinar sua consideração no planejamento e prever tratamento específico para os SAH. Ademais, abriu espaço para procedimentos de licenciamento de empreendimentos estratégicos distintos e reconheceu o valor sistêmico desse sistema de armazenamento. As Resoluções Normativas ANEEL nºs 1.161/2026 e 1.162/2026 deram tratamento a diferentes configurações de SAH incluindo do tipo ciclo fechado e intervenções associadas a usinas hidroelétricas existentes. As Resoluções CNPE nºs 7/2026 e 8/2026, por sua vez, orientaram a identificação de projetos e a estruturação de mecanismos competitivos para a contratação dos SAH. Recentemente, a Portaria Normativa MME nº 143/2026 estabeleceu o cronograma estimado de leilões para 2027 a 2029 e previu a possibilidade de participação de SAH nos Leilões de Reserva de Capacidade (LRCap) na forma de potência. A perspectiva de contratação deixa, assim, de ser apenas uma diretriz regulatória e passa a estar associada a uma programação concreta de leilões, ainda condicionada às necessidades de potência identificadas pela EPE. A fim de dar mais consistência e fundamentação à contratação via leilões, a EPE estruturou uma metodologia de cadastramento de projetos para subsidiar a definição do desenho dos futuros leilões. Isto porque o armazenamento hidrológico, diferentemente das baterias, não constitui, por si só, um produto homogêneo. Um SAH voltado a ciclos diários atende a uma necessidade distinta daquele destinado a deslocar excedentes por vários dias. Potência, duração, rampas, frequência de acionamento, ciclos sucessivos e requisitos de controle de frequência e tensão influenciam projetos e seus custos. O edital deverá estabelecer atributos e premissas operacionais claros, permitindo comparar projetos em bases equivalentes e precificar riscos a partir de referências comuns. Para os SAH, o padrão de utilização também afeta dimensionamento, manutenção e risco. Portanto, o contrato deve definir tanto a potência disponível quanto as condições de sua utilização. A alocação de riscos é igualmente decisiva. O risco de construção é do empreendedor, enquanto questões diretamente determinadas pela necessidade do sistema, como o acionamento para bombeamento, precisam de regras claras de liquidação. Também será necessário definir o tratamento da energia consumida no bombeamento, sua exposição ao Preço de Liquidação das Diferenças (PLD) e interação com o Mecanismo de Realocação de Energia (MRE). É importante que o consumo associado ao bombeamento não seja confundido com o risco hidrológico compartilhado pelo MRE e que geração e bombeamento tenham tratamento contábil específico na Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), além de evitar dupla incidência da compensação financeira pelo uso dos recursos hídricos. artigo.texto: Do carbono medido ao ganho ambiental comprovado: O desafio do SBCE Medir emissões não é, por si só, comprovar ganho ambiental. A partir da nova portaria do SBCE, o artigo propõe critérios para que a prova científica sustente conclusões jurídicas legítimas. segunda-feira, 9 de novembro de 2026 Atualizado às 17:21 Introdução Uma indústria divulga um inventário de emissões verificado por terceira parte. Um projeto florestal documenta o aumento do carbono armazenado na vegetação. Os dois resultados são relevantes. Mas bastam para afirmar que houve redução adicional de emissões ou ganho ambiental comprovado? Não necessariamente. O inventário quantifica emissões em determinado perímetro; o levantamento de biomassa descreve um atributo da vegetação. Nenhuma dessas evidências, isoladamente, demonstra causalidade, recuperação da biodiversidade ou saldo ecológico líquido. Essa distinção tem efeitos concretos sobre certificações, decisões de investimento e confiança nas informações ambientais. É nesse contexto que ganha relevância a portaria SEMC/MF 3.199, de 28 de outubro de 2026, publicada no dia seguinte. Ao escalonar as obrigações de mensuração, relato e verificação - MRV no SBCE - Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa, a norma cria condições para produzir informações climáticas comparáveis e sujeitas a controle. Não fixa, de imediato, limites individuais de emissão nem impõe aquisição generalizada de créditos. Mas torna urgente uma pergunta para a regulação climática: o que cada metodologia permite reconhecer, juridicamente, como resultado ambiental comprovado? A resposta exige congruência entre o fato a demonstrar, a aptidão do método e a extensão da conclusão extraída da evidência. 1. A portaria 3.199/26 e a regulação orientada por evidências A portaria organiza três momentos sucessivos em cada etapa setorial. No primeiro ano (A1), prevê a apresentação do plano de monitoramento; no segundo (A2), a mensuração das emissões e remoções segundo o plano aprovado; a partir do terceiro (A3), a mensuração continua e passa a ser acompanhada da apresentação do relatório verificado referente ao ano anterior (art. 2º). O primeiro grupo começa em 2027; os demais têm início previsto até 2029 e até 2031, respectivamente (art. 3º). Conteúdo, formato e prazos de entrega ainda serão detalhados em atos próprios, editados com a antecedência mínima estabelecida pelo parágrafo único do art. 2º. O escalonamento não equivale a enquadramento automático pelo CNAE. Os §§ 2º e 3º do art. 3º exigem considerar as atividades, fontes e instalações efetivamente abrangidas. Além disso, a lei 15.042/24 prevê, no art. 30, patamares superiores a 10 mil toneladas de CO2 equivalente por ano para as obrigações de plano e relato e superiores a 25 mil para a conciliação periódica, observadas as condições legais e a regulamentação. A portaria organiza o calendário do MRV; não antecipa, por si, as obrigações de entrega de ativos decorrentes de um plano de alocação. A sequência normativa é coerente. O art. 29 prevê os deveres dos operadores; o art. 32 disciplina o relato anual e sua avaliação de conformidade; e o art. 30, § 2º, condiciona a aplicação das obrigações às atividades para as quais existam metodologias consolidadas de MRV. O art. 5º, V, por sua vez, exige uma estrutura confiável, consistente e transparente, apta a assegurar a integridade e a comparabilidade das informações. A qualidade da mensuração deixa, assim, de ser um detalhe instrumental: integra as condições jurídicas para operacionalizar deveres quantitativos. A própria lei separa, contudo, etapas que poderiam parecer equivalentes. Segundo o art. 1º, § 5º, remoções superiores às emissões não se convertem automaticamente em Certificados de Redução ou Remoção Verificada de Emissões (CRVEs). O art. 44 condiciona o reconhecimento desses ativos a metodologia credenciada, mensuração e relato, verificação independente e inscrição no Registro Central. Inventariar emissões, verificar declarações e reconhecer um resultado apto a gerar ativo regulado são operações diferentes. O legislador não atribui efeitos idênticos a informações que respondem a finalidades distintas. 2. O que os estudos científicos demonstram - E o que não demonstram A distinção entre informação mensurada e efeito efetivamente atribuível a uma intervenção não é apenas teórica. Probst e colaboradores (2024), em síntese publicada na Nature Communications, examinaram estudos de avaliação rigorosa referentes a 2.346 projetos de mitigação. Estimaram que menos de 16% dos créditos emitidos nos projetos avaliados correspondiam a reduções efetivas de emissões. O percentual varia entre modalidades e não representa todo o universo de projetos. Mais importante: a pesquisa examina a integridade do creditamento e da adicionalidade, não a acurácia geral dos inventários corporativos que o SBCE passará a exigir. Em direção complementar, Swinfield e colaboradores (2026) reuniram seis avaliações independentes de 44 projetos REDD+. Em 36 deles, as estimativas apontaram redução do desmatamento; ainda assim, o desmatamento evitado reivindicado superou, no agregado, em 10,7 vezes aquele sustentado pelas avaliações independentes. O resultado não autoriza afirmar que a conservação financiada por esses mecanismos seja inútil. Evidencia algo mais preciso: um benefício pode ser real sem que sua magnitude declarada esteja causalmente demonstrada. Linhas de base, áreas de comparação e modelos contrafactuais afetam decisivamente essa atribuição. Outro limite aparece quando se altera o objeto da pergunta. Ong e colaboradores (2026), na Nature Climate Change, examinaram 133 projetos de desmatamento evitado por meio de cinco indicadores de integridade ecológica e controles comparáveis. Predominaram resultados mistos, insignificantes ou negativos segundo os indicadores adotados. artigo.texto: A comprehensive academic review published in Frontiers in Chemistry outlines how precise chemical fluorination transforms carbon nanotubes from inert conductive platforms into highly reactive components for advanced electrochemical energy storage. Writing across a framework linking synthesis routes, chemical bonding, structural evolution, and device performance, the researchers show that attaching fluorine atoms to one-dimensional carbon tubular lattices provides an exceptionally direct mechanism for manipulating electronic structure, surface polarity, and interfacial reactivity. The incorporation of fluorine replaces sp2-hybridized carbon networks with fluorinated sp3 local environments, generating a spectrum of semi-ionic and covalent carbon-fluorine bonds. Because pristine carbon nanotubes inherently feature chemically inert surfaces, restricted electrochemically active sites, and poor wettability toward polar ether- and carbonate-based battery electrolytes, chemical modification has become essential for expanding their roles beyond standard passive conductive additives. The structural characteristics and electrochemical utility of fluorinated carbon nanotubes depend decisively on the synthetic route used to introduce the halogen atoms, as different fluorination methods operate under distinct kinetic, thermal, and mass-transport regimes. Direct gas-phase fluorination utilizing pure fluorine gas or diluted fluorine-nitrogen mixtures at elevated temperatures between 200 °C and 600 °C remains the most common industrial method, enabling high fluorine loadings with fluorine-to-carbon atomic ratios approaching 0.8 to 1.0. However, because molecular fluorine has a kinetic diameter of approximately 0.35 nanometers, diffusion within tightly packed nanotube bundles is restricted, leading to localized over-fluorination, outer-wall exfoliation, and severe lattice disruption. Conversely, atomic fluorination driven by the thermal decomposition of xenon difluoride or terbium tetrafluoride releases atomic fluorine radicals with a van der Waals radius of roughly 0.147 nanometers. These smaller species access nanotube surfaces without mass-transfer barriers, yielding exceptionally homogeneous fluorine distributions dominated by semi-ionic configurations while preserving the structural integrity of the graphitic core. Alternative low-temperature and liquid-phase fluorination techniques offer further synthetic control by tailoring reactive species and functional penetration depths. Radio-frequency or microwave plasma fluorination using carbon tetrafluoride operates below 150 °C, generating reactive radicals and ionic fragments that are confined to the outermost atomic shells of the carbon nanotubes. This selective surface modification introduces carbon-fluorine, difluoromethylene, and trifluoromethyl groups while keeping the conductive inner graphitic channels intact, yielding modest fluorine contents below a fluorine-to-carbon ratio of 0.3 that enhance interfacial polarity without degrading electrical pathways. Liquid-phase routes, including solvothermal treatments with electrophilic Selectfluor at temperatures from 140 °C to 200 °C or nucleophilic room-temperature reactions with aqueous hydrofluoric acid, provide milder reaction environments that favor semi-ionic bond configurations. Additionally, solid-state pyrolytic techniques employing fluorine-donating precursors such as polytetrafluoroethylene or ammonium fluoride at 400 °C to 700 °C introduce low concentrations of fluorine without requiring corrosive gaseous reagents. Spectroscopic investigations resolve the intricate evolution of local chemical environments as fluorine accumulates on the carbon nanotube framework. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy distinguishes semi-ionic carbon-fluorine vibrations near 1110 reciprocal centimeters from covalent carbon-fluorine stretching bands appearing at 1210 to 1220 reciprocal centimeters, alongside difluoromethylene features emerging near 1340 reciprocal centimeters under deeper fluorination conditions. Complementary X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies semi-ionic species by carbon 1s binding energies between 288.2 and 288.8 electronvolts and fluorine 1s peaks between 685.5 and 687.0 electronvolts, whereas covalent bonds emerge at higher carbon 1s energies of 289.4 to 290.4 electronvolts and fluorine 1s signals between 688.0 and 689.0 electronvolts. Solid-state fluorine-19 magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance tracking demonstrates that semi-ionic configurations resonate near minus 152 parts per million, whereas strong covalent bonds appear near minus 190 parts per million and undergo downfield shifts toward minus 188 parts per million when fluorination temperatures increase from 350 °C to 430 °C, directly reflecting a progressive loss of ionic character and a strengthening of covalent bonding. Lattice alterations and morphological reconstructions driven by fluorination fundamentally reshape both physical dimensions and electronic transport within carbon nanotubes. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals that fluorination expands the pristine graphitic interlayer spacing of 0.33 nanometers up to 0.67 nanometers in heavily treated outer walls while inner shells retain their native graphitic dimensions. Raman spectroscopy reflects this structural reorganization through increases in the defect-associated D-band to graphitic G-band intensity ratio, caused by the conversion of sp2 carbon into sp3 hybridization. Because extended covalent carbon-fluorine bonding interrupts electron delocalization across the carbon framework, electrical conductivity drops drastically as fluorine content rises. artigo.texto: A Nvidia fechou o trimestre encerrado em julho de 2026 com receita de US$ 96,2 bilhões, avanço de 106% sobre igual intervalo do ano anterior, e mais de 92% desse montante veio de um único segmento: os data centers. Mais de nove décimos do faturamento dependem de um só tipo de cliente — quem compra capacidade de computação para inteligência artificial. A comparação recorrente com os vendedores de pás da corrida do ouro tem fundamento: a companhia não precisa acertar qual modelo de IA vai dominar, porque vende o equipamento que praticamente todos os concorrentes precisam comprar. Microsoft, Google e Meta figuram entre as empresas cujas tecnologias rodam sobre processadores da Nvidia, conforme a fonte. Data centers respondem por mais de 92% da receita Fundada em 1993, na Califórnia, a Nvidia começou projetando processadores gráficos para computadores pessoais e videogames. O salto veio quando a mesma arquitetura usada para renderizar imagens se mostrou eficiente em tarefas de cálculo pesado — sobretudo o treinamento de modelos de inteligência artificial. GPU é a sigla de unidade de processamento gráfico: o chip projetado para executar milhares de contas em paralelo, e não em sequência. Semicondutor, por sua vez, é o material cuja condução elétrica é controlada para processar informação; no vocabulário do setor, o termo virou sinônimo do próprio chip. Projeta o chip, mas não tem fábrica A Nvidia opera no modelo fabless — desenha o produto e entrega a fabricação a terceiros. Quem produz a maior parte dos chips avançados é a taiwanesa TSMC. O arranjo dispensa fábricas próprias e cria um elo único na cadeia: um problema na produção taiwanesa chega rápido ao volume de vendas, enquanto o clima entre China e Taiwan segue no radar. Do videogame ao data center O peso do portfólio não está em cada item isolado, e sim na integração: chip, rede e software são vendidos como um sistema. CUDA, o ambiente de programação da empresa, amarra o desenvolvedor ao seu ecossistema — e essa combinação é o que dificulta a substituição por um fornecedor alternativo. A concorrência inclui os próprios clientes A AMD, com a linha Instinct, é a rival mais direta no mercado de aceleradores para IA e servidores. Do outro lado aparece a Huawei: os processadores Ascend ganharam espaço como alternativa chinesa aos chips americanos, movimento reforçado pelas restrições de exportação impostas por Washington. Google e Amazon, dois grandes compradores, desenvolvem silício próprio — TPUs no caso do Google e a linha Trainium na nuvem AWS — para cortar custos e reduzir dependência de terceiros. A Intel segue na disputa por processadores de servidor. Quatro riscos que a concentração escancara - Fornecedor único: a produção concentrada na TSMC transforma qualquer ruptura em risco de entrega. - Geopolítica: as limitações dos EUA à exportação de chips avançados para a China fecham parte de um mercado relevante e estimulam alternativas locais. - Ciclo de gastos: se o investimento em data centers perder ritmo, a demanda pelos processadores recua junto. - Clientes verticalizados: quanto mais os chips próprios de Google, Amazon e outros avançarem, maior a pressão sobre preço e participação de mercado da Nvidia. O episódio que derrubou as ações Um suposto caso de espionagem chinesa envolvendo o fundador e CEO Jensen Huang deu origem a uma investigação, derrubou os papéis e recolocou no debate a vulnerabilidade das gigantes de IA depois de valorizações bilionárias. A reação tende a anteceder qualquer conclusão da apuração — e diz menos sobre o mérito do caso do que sobre o volume de expectativa embutido no preço. O que muda para quem acompanha a empresa Com a receita praticamente toda atrelada a um único destino, o balanço da Nvidia passa a espelhar o ciclo de investimento das grandes plataformas de nuvem. Um arrefecimento desses gastos não reduz apenas a taxa de crescimento: atinge quase toda a base de receita de uma vez. Historicamente, empresas com faturamento concentrado em um único cliente final costumam apresentar resultados mais sensíveis a revisões de orçamento do setor. Para quem acompanha o papel, dois indicadores carregam mais informação do que a cotação do dia: a evolução da receita de data centers e o grau de adoção dos chips próprios desenvolvidos pelos clientes. O primeiro mede a força do ciclo; o segundo antecipa a pressão competitiva que pode corroer preço e participação.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Por que o Brasil está atraindo investimentos bilionários em data centers? Publicado 07/11/2026 • 09:00 | Atualizado há 2 dias KEY POINTS Foto: pexels Ações de empresas de centros de dados de IA ficaram sob pressão após democratas conquistarem vitórias expressivas nas midterms. O Brasil vem ganhando espaço na disputa global por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA). Enquanto comunidades nos Estados Unidos pressionam contra a construção de novos data centers, o país oferece incentivos fiscais, energia elétrica mais barata e um mercado consumidor em expansão para atrair gigantes como Amazon, Google e Microsoft. Uma reportagem publicada pela Revista Fortune, destaca que essa combinação favorece a expansão do setor no país. Além disso, a Lei REDATA, sancionada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em setembro, reduziu impostos sobre equipamentos de data centers e estabeleceu contrapartidas para estimular a pesquisa e o desenvolvimento no Brasil. Leia também: Imposto Seletivo deve começar em fevereiro de 2027; governo prevê manter IPI na transição O tamanho do mercado brasileiro já aparece nos planos das grandes empresas de tecnologia. A Amazon Web Services (AWS) investiu mais de US$ 3,8 bilhões (cerca de R$ 20,7 bilhões) em infraestrutura de data centers na região desde 2011. A companhia também prometeu investir outros US$ 1,8 bilhão (R$ 9,8 bilhões) até 2034. O Google pretende dobrar sua infraestrutura de computação em nuvem no Brasil até 2030, em resposta ao aumento da demanda. Já a Microsoft comprometeu US$ 2,7 bilhões (R$ 14,7 bilhões) para ampliar sua infraestrutura de nuvem e inteligência artificial ao longo de três anos. Embora a demanda local ainda impulsione grande parte da expansão na América Latina, Carlos Barrera, CEO da Atlas Renewable Energy, avalia que a região também pode receber investimentos que encontram dificuldades para avançar nos Estados Unidos. Outro atrativo é o custo da eletricidade. A energia no Brasil custa menos da metade do preço praticado nos Estados Unidos. De acordo com dados do Ministério de Minas e Energia, quase 87% da eletricidade brasileira vem de fontes renováveis. A expansão das usinas eólicas e solares também contribuiu para gerar excedentes de energia. Esse cenário favorece os data centers, que precisam de fornecimento constante de eletricidade para manter servidores e equipamentos de processamento em funcionamento. Entretanto, a vantagem pode enfrentar obstáculos. O Brasil precisará ampliar as linhas de transmissão para conectar os grandes empreendimentos à rede elétrica. Além disso, autoridades discutem os possíveis efeitos desses projetos nas contas de luz dos consumidores. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC A carga tributária brasileira também representava um desafio para o setor, já que os impostos federais sobre equipamentos importados elevavam os custos de construção. Para enfrentar o problema, Lula sancionou, em 15 de setembro, a Lei REDATA, que reduz impostos sobre equipamentos destinados a data centers que cumpram os requisitos legais. Em contrapartida, as empresas precisam oferecer pelo menos 10% dos serviços de computação qualificados a clientes brasileiros e investir 2% do valor dos equipamentos beneficiados em pesquisa e desenvolvimento no país. A iniciativa busca fortalecer a soberania digital. Segundo o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, 60% dos dados digitais brasileiros ainda são processados no exterior. Com mais capacidade computacional instalada localmente, o governo espera estimular empresas nacionais a desenvolver soluções de IA e reduzir a dependência de serviços estrangeiros. Apesar das oportunidades, a expansão dos data centers também enfrenta resistência. Poucos dias antes da entrada em vigor da REDATA, procuradores federais acionaram a Justiça contra um projeto ligado ao TikTok. Leia também: Ibovespa abre em queda e recua aos 165 mil pontos, com dólar a R$ 5,50 e juros em alta A ação exigiu um estudo de impacto ambiental e consulta ao povo indígena Anacé antes do início das operações. O episódio mostra que a atração de investimentos precisa considerar os efeitos dos empreendimentos sobre o meio ambiente e as comunidades próximas. Assim, o Brasil reúne condições para ampliar sua participação no mercado global de inteligência artificial. artigo.texto: Céu noturno: rastros de satélites podem interferir em imagens captadas por observatórios astronômicos (Freepik) Redatora Publicado em 9 de novembro de 2026 às 12h00. A expansão de data centers no espaço pode transformar a aparência do céu noturno e prejudicar pesquisas astronômicas realizadas na Terra. Cientistas alertam que projetos envolvendo centenas de milhares de satélites poderão aumentar a poluição luminosa e dificultar a observação de estrelas, galáxias e outros objetos celestes. O problema já afeta o Observatório Vera C. Rubin, no Chile, onde satélites deixam rastros luminosos nas imagens captadas pelos telescópios. A instalação iniciou em 2026 um levantamento do Universo previsto para durar dez anos. Segundo informações do The Wall Street Journal, astrônomos temem que a expansão das megaconstelações de satélites comprometa parte das observações científicas. O próprio Observatório Vera C. Rubin reconhece que os rastros provocados por satélites representam um desafio para suas pesquisas. Os satélites refletem a luz solar em direção à Terra. Quando atravessam o campo de visão de um telescópio, podem deixar faixas brilhantes nas imagens. Esses rastros dificultam a identificação de objetos celestes e podem comprometer informações utilizadas em pesquisas astronômicas. Segundo Jonathan McDowell, astrofísico que acompanha lançamentos orbitais, existem atualmente mais de 17 mil satélites ativos ao redor da Terra. Há uma década, eram aproximadamente mil. O pesquisador estima que esse número possa ultrapassar 100 mil nos próximos dez anos. Para J. Anthony Tyson, cientista-chefe do Observatório Rubin, a proliferação de satélites representa uma ameaça ao trabalho científico desenvolvido na instalação. Atualmente, grande parte dos satélites em órbita é utilizada para telecomunicações, incluindo o fornecimento de internet pela Starlink, da SpaceX. Entretanto, empresas como SpaceX, Google, Blue Origin e Cowboy Space anunciaram projetos relacionados à instalação de centros de processamento de dados no espaço. Essas estruturas poderiam exigir grandes quantidades de satélites para realizar operações computacionais fora da Terra. A SpaceX apresentou planos para um sistema orbital chamado Starmind, que poderia reunir mais de um milhão de satélites. A empresa também descreveu equipamentos com até 1.500 metros quadrados de área. Já a Cowboy Space apresentou projetos de satélites com aproximadamente 4.800 metros quadrados. As dimensões são superiores às dos satélites Starlink atuais, que possuem cerca de quatro metros quadrados. Uma das preocupações dos pesquisadores envolve o posicionamento dos futuros satélites em órbitas que permitam maior exposição à luz solar. Essas configurações poderiam manter os equipamentos iluminados durante longos períodos, aumentando a quantidade de luz refletida em direção à Terra. Samantha Lawler, professora da Universidade de Regina, no Canadá, alerta que satélites destinados a data centers orbitais poderiam apresentar brilho comparável ao de Vênus. Segundo a pesquisadora, centenas de milhares desses equipamentos poderiam dificultar a visualização da Via Láctea e de estrelas menos brilhantes em determinados horários. Hanno Rein, professor da Universidade de Toronto, também estudou os possíveis efeitos da expansão das constelações. De acordo com suas projeções, parte dos pontos luminosos observados no céu poderia corresponder a satélites artificiais, e não a estrelas. Shane Ross, professor de engenharia da Virginia Tech, desenvolveu uma simulação para representar como uma grande constelação de satélites poderia aparecer vista da superfície terrestre. O modelo mostra milhares de pontos luminosos distribuídos em uma faixa que atravessa o céu, de um horizonte ao outro. A projeção considera um cenário com centenas de milhares de satélites e ilustra como a concentração desses equipamentos poderia alterar a paisagem noturna. A União Astronômica Internacional (IAU) recomenda que os satélites sejam suficientemente pouco brilhantes para não serem visíveis a olho nu. As orientações buscam reduzir a interferência das constelações nas observações astronômicas. Apesar disso, não existem limites regulatórios gerais para o brilho visível dos satélites, segundo as informações apresentadas pelo Observatório Rubin. A SpaceX já adotou medidas voluntárias para reduzir o brilho dos equipamentos Starlink. Tyson afirma que a empresa mantém conversas com pesquisadores sobre o problema há quase uma década. O observatório também relata contatos com outras companhias do setor. Mesmo com essas iniciativas, o crescimento das constelações continua sendo motivo de preocupação. O Observatório Vera C. Rubin iniciou em 2026 um levantamento de dez anos destinado a investigar diferentes fenômenos do Universo. Entre os objetivos estão o estudo da matéria escura, a identificação de asteroides e o acompanhamento de mudanças no céu. A presença crescente de satélites pode dificultar a coleta de imagens e a identificação de objetos menos brilhantes. Tyson teme que a expansão das megaconstelações prejudique a continuidade das observações planejadas. Além dos rastros luminosos nas fotografias, o cientista alerta para a possibilidade de um aumento generalizado do brilho do céu, caso grandes quantidades de satélites sejam colocadas em órbita.

artigo.texto: Opposition to AI data center helped to fuel the nationwide "blue wave" on Election Night for Democrats at the ballot box. This summer, New York became the first in the nation to pass a one-year statewide moratorium on new data center construction. The push continues for Gov. Kathy Hochul to sign more restrictive legislation that passed the state legislature back in June. “Seeing the wins across New York state and the country is a signal that many of the things we’ve been talking about are incredibly popular,” said Democratic state Sen. Kristen Gonzalez. Gonzalez’s Responsible Data Center Development Act passed the state legislature in June. The following month, Hochul signed the nation’s first one-year moratorium on new data centers in New York state. Advocates maintain Gonzalez’s measure covers a broader range of large facilities starting at 20 megawatts or more. The governor’s moratorium has a threshold of 50 megawatts or more. Gonzalez believes data centers helping to fuel turnout nationwide makes her case stronger in having Hochul sign her legislation. “I absolutely think that’s the case,” she said. “We always knew that data centers was a bipartisan issue across the country, but even in New York state. A recent poll said that 63% of New Yorkers would support our moratorium being extended at the end of the one year.” In a statement to Spectrum News 1, a spokesperson for Hochul’s office said in part: "New Yorkers across the state have made abundantly clear that the rapid growth of AI and data centers cannot come at their expense. Governor Hochul listened, acted and is proud to have delivered the first data center moratorium in the nation. The Governor will continue to strengthen protections around artificial intelligence that will put New Yorker's and their future first." Critics argue stricter guidelines on data centers will come at an economic expense, with some states missing out on investments. Political expert Grant Reeher says it will depend on if this issue gets worked out on the national level. “If it remains something states are taking different positions, I think the states that aren’t doing it will pay some sort of economic price,” he said. Reeher says he believes what we’ve witnessed at the ballot box in reference to data centers is a “physical proxy” about voters’ much more “general anxiety about the future when it comes to AI.” In a CBS 60 Minutes interview on Sunday, President Donald Trump explained why he’s an advocate for AI data centers. “The level of power of winning that race is very important,” said Trump. “China has no problem with data centers. China has no problem with electricity. By the way, neither do we because I’m demanding that they build their own electric plant.” Despite the arguments, Gonzalez is continuing to advocate. In August, she embarked on a statewide data center tour. On Tuesday, her tour will stop at the First Unitarian Church of Rochester. The event is in partnership with Democratic state Sen. Samara Brouk.

artigo.texto: Jefferson County leaders hold workshop to discuss potential data center impacts Commissioners have seven more months before the county’s data center moratorium, which was put in place this summer, is up MONTICELLO, Fla. (WCTV) - Jefferson County residents and leaders are discussing the potential impacts of data centers as the county’s 12-month moratorium remains in place. County Manager Doug Baber said the workshop on Monday was an opportunity for commissioners to hear from experts about the potential impacts of data centers. “Data centers have been known as the boogeyman for quite a while, and I don’t disagree with a lot of that stuff because it’s unknown,” Baber said. “We want to make sure we bring in the experts on both sides of the field to talk about how much water it would use, how much electricity it would demand, how many acres they would have to have, how many jobs they create per acre.” Attorneys and professors from Florida State University and the University of Florida were among several experts sharing their knowledge, including the potential costs of studying the impacts. Andrew Fay, an attorney with the Digital Infrastructure Industry Group at Greenberg Traurig, discussed the cost of engineering studies needed to help commissioners make informed decisions. “The cost for the engineering studies for the expertise to make a decision on the impacts for water, the impacts that maybe the noise will have on the area, the light, the impact to the natural environment that it could be built in, all are extremely expensive and can be extremely time-consuming,” Fay said. Experts discussed both the potential jobs data centers could bring and concerns about light, noise and water. More news out of the Big Bend: Those concerns resonated with District Four Commissioner Austin Hosford, who pointed to issues residents have already raised about the Trulieve cannabis facility in the county. “Just right off the top, hearing the issues in these other places Texas, Virginia, light, noise, and water. I know how aware y’all are of what we’ve been dealing with in Jefferson County; we’ve got a major operation that has caused light, noise, and water problems for quite a lot of people, so that jumps off to me big time,” Hosford said. Residents also had a chance to ask questions and share their concerns, with many worried a data center could change the county’s rural character. Jefferson County is known for its natural resources, including the Wacissa River and springs. Some residents questioned whether the community has the resources to support a data center. “We don’t have the baseline to support it. Tallahassee could. We just don’t have it. I don’t see how it benefits us long term. I’m not opposed to data centers; I just don’t see how our county could support the construction of it or even the employment that we really want from it,” Jefferson County resident Tracy Place Allison II said. Baber also said there have been no applications for data centers in Jefferson County. No action was taken Monday night. Commissioners have seven more months before the county’s data center moratorium, which was put in place this summer, is up. artigo.texto: [SMM ESS Flash] A Revolta da Alemanha comissiona a primeira bateria doméstica de íons de sódio de 10 kWh, alocação de 2026 esgotada A startup Revolta, sediada em Frankfurt, instalou e comissionou a primeira bateria doméstica de íons de sódio de 10 kWh da Alemanha em uma propriedade perto de Aschaffenburg, um sistema com tensão nominal de 450 V composto por cinco módulos de 2 kWh combinados com um inversor SMA. Cada módulo pesa 18,7 kg, com classificação de proteção IP64 e densidade de energia de 107 Wh/kg e 141 Wh/l, carrega e descarrega a 0,4 C, o que corresponde a cerca de 2,5 horas, e a configuração de 10 kWh entrega uma potência máxima de cerca de 4 kW; a propriedade também abriga cerca de 20 kW de energia solar fotovoltaica e uma pequena central hidrelétrica convertida de um antigo moinho. A empresa enquadra a instalação como o início de seu lançamento comercial, permanecendo ainda em estágio piloto, com mais sistemas piloto em locais selecionados de clientes na Alemanha planejados para as próximas semanas e medidores gratuitos fornecidos para coletar dados operacionais; os módulos são listados a EUR 599 cada e o conjunto de cinco módulos de 10 kWh a EUR 2.995, com a alocação de 2026 esgotada e reservas abertas para 2027. Potência nominal, vida útil de ciclo e números de eficiência não foram divulgados, e os primeiros dados operacionais reais de armazenamento doméstico de íons de sódio na Alemanha fornecerão amostras de validação para desempenho em baixas temperaturas e segurança.

artigo.texto: After pushback, Ottawa voters approve 10-year moratorium on data centers Ottawa residents voted overwhelmingly to impose a 10-year moratorium on data centers, joining a national trend of communities restricting data centers on the November Ballot. After pushback, Ottawa voters approve 10-year moratorium on data centers Ottawa residents voted overwhelmingly to impose a 10-year moratorium on data centers, joining a national trend of communities restricting data centers on the November Ballot. Ottawa, Kansas, residents voted by over 70% to approve a 10-year moratorium on data centers following a lengthy back-and-forth between county residents, city officials, and third party spending. It started when a proposal for a data center popped up just on the outside of Ottawa. Franklin County resident, Jessica Christopher, brought her concerns to the city. "When they had discussed putting up this 450 megawatt or whatever data center, it was going to be about a mile from my house," Christopher said. Christopher and other residents began to feel their concerns about the project were not being met. So they started petitioning to let voters weigh in on the issue, under Kansas law. "We rallied the troops. We went and did a few drive-thru events. And when I was sitting there counting the last ones, we had 1031 (signatures)," Christopher said. Despite gathering significant support, Christopher said the group faced obstacles. City officials argued the petition could not make it onto the ballot, as it was an administrative issue and not a legislative. That's when Ottawa residents, including Michael Lewis, sued the city. "We filed for a writ of mandamus, which what that says is that's compelling your elected officials to do their job since their job was to put it on the ballot or accept it. They didn't do their job. The district clerk or district court judge ruled that, yes, the citizens do deserve to be heard," Lewis said. The efforts surrounding the issue led to the formation of Ottawa United, a group of residents focused on the issue of data centers. "It was a mix between Republicans and Democrats and a bunch of unaffiliated voters. And we all just came together for a common good, which is why we named it Ottawa United," Chirstopher said. The campaign also faced challenges from outside influences. KMBC 9 uncovered tens of thousands of dollars in campaign filings from a Virginia-based political action committee, called the Defend US PAC. The PAC spending focused on urging residents to vote no on data center issues in Kansas communities, including in Ottawa and Emporia. "There was at least five or six different mailers that showed up at the doors. We had text messages come in every week," Lewis said. On election day, voters approved the moratorium in Ottawa by just over 70%. "I broke down, it was amazing. It was the thing that I have made that I am the proudest of, other than my children," Christopher said. Ottawa joins other Kansas communities, and communities across the U.S., in addressing the controversial issue of data center development. "It was kind of nice not only winning for our community, but also pushing back to the big money interests, saying that we're not for sale," Lewis said.
