artigo.texto: O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, propôs cortar de 25% para 15% o imposto corporativo para projetos de inteligência artificial com investimento mínimo de US$ 1 bilhão para transformar a Patagônia em polo de data centers. O Brasil já lidera a região nesse mercado. Em Los Toldos, na estepe patagônica, um data center de 12 MW já funciona com gás que seria queimado como subproduto da extração de petróleo de xisto, segundo o Financial Times, reproduzido pela Folha. Tomás Ocampo, fundador da Unblock Energy, planeja uma instalação de várias centenas de MW na zona rural argentina. Ele diz ter recebido uma enxurrada de ligações de investidores dos Estados Unidos após as eleições de meio de mandato americanas. "Antes de colocarmos data centers no oceano e no espaço, a Argentina faz muito sentido", disse Ocampo. Como fica o incentivo fiscal argentino O corte de imposto vale para projetos com investimento mínimo de US$ 1 bilhão e ainda depende de aprovação no Senado argentino, que também avalia o projeto Green Capital, em Chubut, com US$ 3 bilhões em 130 mil hectares. O consumo de eletricidade estimado é de 2,7 vezes todo o consumo de Buenos Aires em 2025, dado que já alimenta a resistência de moradores da região. Publicidade Não vamos regulamentar a inteligência artificial. Vamos deixá-la livre. A frase foi dita por Milei em reunião da Câmara de Comércio dos EUA. A oposição no Congresso argentino já modificou regras sobre compra de terras por estrangeiros e travou a autorização para que sistemas de IA administrem empresas sem presença humana. Como o Brasil já sai na frente O Brasil concentra 48% da capacidade de data centers em operação na América Latina e 71% de tudo que está em construção na região, segundo levantamento da Forbes Brasil. O país deve atrair US$ 33 bilhões até 2030. O país também concentra três das cinco maiores posições regionais em capacidade instalada, à frente de México, Chile e Colômbia. O avanço brasileiro pode render US$ 60 bilhões por ano até 2050, e o setor cresce no país enquanto trava nos Estados Unidos. A disputa pela água que data centers consomem também é tema no Brasil. Um estudo mostrou que as instalações de IA em São Paulo usam 16,1 bilhões de litros de água por ano, preocupação que também mobiliza moradores da Patagônia. O que acontece agora O projeto de incentivos segue em tramitação no Senado argentino, sem data certa de votação. O projeto de maior destaque de Milei na área, anunciado em outubro do ano passado, pode ter estagnado, segundo a Folha. O governo argentino não detalhou um novo cronograma. Grandes empresas de tecnologia, enquanto isso, seguem de olho nos dois países ao mesmo tempo.

artigo.texto: BOISE, Idaho — No mega data centers are currently proposed within Boise city limits, but with large-scale projects emerging elsewhere in Idaho, Mayor Lauren McLean says she doesn't want to wait until one arrives to determine whether the city is prepared. In an interview with Idaho News 6 on Monday, McLean explained what prompted her call for a six-month moratorium on large data center development, what questions she wants answered and why she believes the city needs to act now. "A lot of people are asking that, and they're asking why now, but I wouldn't want them to ask tomorrow, why didn't you do it," McLean said. WATCH: Boise mayor explains preemptive data center pause McLean pointed to recent data center proposals in other Idaho communities as a major factor behind her decision. South of Boise, a developer has proposed a project involving nearly 3,700 acres of federal public land, including a 4 million-square-foot data center. Meta already operates a data center in Kuna, while city leaders in Pocatello recently rejected another large-scale proposal. McLean said developments like those have raised questions about whether Boise has adequate protections in place. "This is a preemptive step. We don't want to be too late, so we're going to get ahead of this and ask the questions we need to ask to make sure we're advocating for Boise," McLean said. Those questions extend beyond the environmental impacts of data centers to whether the facilities provide enough long-term economic benefits for the communities hosting them. "The impact that it would have on water, the power that's needed, the number of jobs that might or might not exist, and also the noise," McLean said. Under her proposal, Boise would temporarily prohibit new data centers larger than 100,000 square feet or requiring more than 20 megawatts of power. The city has no pending applications meeting those thresholds. The proposal also raises questions about how Boise evaluates major industrial development, particularly as the city supports Micron Technology's multi-billion-dollar semiconductor expansion. Like large data centers, semiconductor manufacturing requires significant electricity and water resources. Asked how Micron's expansion differs from the facilities she wants to study, McLean emphasized the company's commitment to permanent jobs and investment in Boise. "Micron is not a data center," McLean said. "Yes, they require water, power. They're investing in the community, and they're creating opportunity for our kids and grandkids to come home with high-paying jobs." Her response highlights another consideration the city intends to examine: whether the economic benefits of large data centers justify their demands on local infrastructure and resources. McLean said she wants Boise to attract companies that invest in the community and provide lasting employment opportunities. Rather than responding to a specific development application, McLean said the proposed moratorium would allow city officials to study potential impacts before deciding what long-term regulations may be necessary. She also wants residents involved in determining what protections the city should establish. "Part of the six months is going to be a conversation with the community. I want to hear from residents on what they expect," McLean said. Asked whether six months would provide enough time, McLean said the city intends to use the period to examine existing regulatory tools, identify potential gaps and determine what additional steps may be needed. The mayor also suggested Idaho communities need more support at the state level when evaluating large data center developments. "The state needs to create guardrails so that communities can advocate for themselves," McLean said. For now, McLean's proposal is less about responding to a project already seeking approval in Boise and more about determining what rules should be in place if one eventually arrives. The Boise City Council will hold a public hearing on the proposed moratorium Tuesday, Nov. 10, before considering whether to approve it.

artigo.texto: Land & Expand: Texas’ AI Boom Meets a New Political Reality Key Highlights - Democrat Gina Hinojosa's election as Texas governor, alongside Democratic gains in the state House and statewide offices, raises the prospect of an extended data center permitting pause and new legislation in 2027. - Riot Platforms disclosed a 910 MW, approximately $28 billion lease with Anthropic at its Corsicana campus, while Hut 8 advanced its gigawatt-scale Beacon Point project. - CenterPoint Energy increased its 10-year capital plan to $70.7 billion as Greater Houston prepares for major industrial and data center electricity demand. - Fermi's proposed 222 MW TensorWave lease missed its closing deadline, while Microsoft declined to exercise an expansion option for capacity at Nscale's Texas project. - From San Antonio to Hudspeth County, developers increasingly face demands for greater transparency, water and power safeguards, and clearer community benefits. In DCF's Land & Expand series, we track where North American data center development is taking root, where it's accelerating, and the forces shaping which projects actually get built. Today we examine how Texas has become one of the clearest demonstrations of the extraordinary scale of AI infrastructure development — and of the challenges now facing the industry as it attempts to turn that investment into operating capacity. In the space of several weeks, the state has seen major new data center leases, expanded utility investment plans, new behind-the-meter generation proposals, and continued construction on large AI campuses. At the same time, regulators have tightened oversight, municipalities have adopted additional development controls, and several high-profile transactions have encountered financing or execution challenges. Then came the November 3 midterm elections. Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated three-term Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming the first Democrat elected Texas governor since Ann Richards in 1990. Democrats also won the Texas House and the lieutenant governorship, although Republicans retained their majority in the state Senate. The results introduce a new political dimension to a data center market already undergoing substantial regulatory change. Hinojosa made the industry's rapid expansion a campaign issue, calling for a moratorium on new approvals until lawmakers establish stronger protections for communities, water supplies, electricity customers, and local decision-making. In a November 5 interview reported by Reuters, the governor-elect reaffirmed her intention to pause further approvals until those protections are in place. As Data Center Frontier reported in August, Texas was already moving toward a more restrictive regulatory framework under Abbott, who ordered audits of prospective data centers and suspended certain approvals pending the results. Hinojosa's election could extend that process and place new requirements on developers seeking to move projects forward. Yet the state's AI infrastructure market is hardly standing still. The emerging Texas story is not simply one of growth versus regulation. It is about a new set of conditions under which massive capital commitments, available power, established customers, and community acceptance may determine which developments actually reach operation. A $28 Billion Agreement Shows That Texas Is Still in Expansion Mode One of the largest recent transactions illustrates the continuing strength of demand. On November 4, Riot Platforms announced a 15-year, triple-net powered-land lease covering 910 MW of critical IT capacity at its Corsicana campus in Navarro County. Although Riot initially described its customer as a leading frontier AI laboratory, the company's quarterly SEC filing identifies Anthropic as the tenant. Riot estimates that the agreement represents approximately $28 billion in contractual revenue over its initial term, with an average of about $1.8 billion annually. The contract became effective November 4 after the applicable approvals and technical conditions were satisfied. The development model is noteworthy. Riot will provide land, powered pads, and high- and medium-voltage electrical infrastructure, while Anthropic will supply and operate its modular computing equipment. The lease covers a contiguous 332-acre site, with deliveries expected in three phases extending through July 2028. The first phase comprises 400 MW, followed by 200 MW and 310 MW. Under the agreement, Anthropic is responsible for electricity costs and other operating expenses, while Riot retains responsibility for the site's power infrastructure. Rent is structured around contracted capacity rather than actual computing utilization. The result is a substantially more defined commercial arrangement than a speculative gigawatt-scale development announcement. Nevertheless, construction, financing, commissioning, and scheduled delivery remain significant obligations. It is also an example of the changing role of former cryptocurrency infrastructure operators in the AI market. Sites originally assembled around access to large electrical loads are increasingly being repositioned to serve customers requiring high-density computing capacity. The transaction underscores the continuing appetite for large-scale Texas developments, extending the expansion trend documented in DCF's previous Land & Expand roundup. Riot's agreement was announced one day after Hinojosa's election victory. The timing is striking, although the transaction was negotiated and signed before the election and should not be interpreted as a response to its outcome. Instead, it demonstrates the simultaneous forces now shaping Texas: substantial demand for power-ready infrastructure and growing uncertainty over the rules governing future development. artigo.texto: BYD investirá R$ 1 bilhão para produzir vans e caminhões no Brasil Minas Gerais, São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro disputam a próxima unidade da fabricante chinesa, que prevê gerar dois mil empregos A BYD vai instalar uma nova fábrica no Brasil para produzir vans elétricas e caminhões. A coluna apurou com exclusividade para a CNN Brasil que o projeto prevê investimento de R$ 1 bilhão e a criação de 2 mil postos de trabalho entre 2028 e 2029, início da produção. Minas Gerais, São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro foram selecionados pela fabricante e disputam o investimento. A escolha final do estado ainda está em aberto porque virá acompanhada pelo pacote dos incentivos. O projeto marca a segunda fase da expansão industrial da BYD no país. Depois de colocar em operação a fábrica de automóveis de Camaçari, na Bahia. A greentech prepara a nova unidade voltada aos veículos comerciais. Com as vans elétricas, a montadora entra numa disputa com as clássicas, que vendem os modelos a diesel. Durante a semana, a SAIC, com a Volks Caminhões, exibirá sua defesa no segmento das vans, trazendo novidades. Na Fenatran, que começa nesta segunda (9) em São Paulo, a BYD vai trazer os caminhões elétricos eT35 e eT75, além de uma configuração do eT23 para o transporte de bebidas. O eT35 usa a bateria Blade, enquanto o eT75 é voltado à distribuição urbana e regional. Os modelos que sairão da nova fábrica ainda não foram detalhados e devem ser anunciados nos próximos meses. Na Bahia A fábrica de Camaçari ultrapassou 150 mil veículos produzidos e 9,5 mil empregos diretos pouco mais de um ano após a inauguração, segundo balanço divulgado pela montadora em 5 de novembro. O investimento anunciado para o complexo chegou a R$ 11,3 bilhões, ante os R$ 5,5 bilhões informados em julho. A unidade baiana, que produz Dolphin Mini, King, Song Pro e Atto 2, tem capacidade instalada de 150 mil veículos por ano, com previsão de chegar a 300 mil na próxima etapa. A BYD já concluiu as obras civis dos galpões de soldagem e pintura e realiza testes operacionais nas duas áreas. Mais de 1.100 profissionais foram contratados para atuar nessas estruturas, que permitirão incorporar novas etapas da fabricação em Camaçari. Quem vai crescer? A BYD levou seus concessionários a Mendoza, na Argentina, para mostrar os carros que vêm por aí. Mas o recado mais direto da convenção foi para os donos das lojas. Alexandre Baldy, vice-presidente sênior da companhia, deixou claro que, na próxima rodada de expansão da rede no Brasil, vai crescer com a BYD quem mantiver a exclusividade entre as marcas chinesas. Na prática, o grupo que quiser abrir mais pontos de venda com a fabricante terá de deixar as rivais asiáticas fora do portfólio. No encontro, a montadora apresentou um plano com sete lançamentos e novos pontos de venda. Um dos SUVs já tem nome e ano para chegar. O Ti7, antecipado por esta coluna, é um híbrido plug-in boxy de sete lugares confirmado para 2027. Com carroceria de linhas quadradas e porte do Denza B5, ele coloca a BYD na disputa por compradores de modelos como o Jetour T2 e o GWM Haval H7. O Dolphin GT será o próximo nacional e nós já cravamos aqui na CNN sobre o híbrido plug-in flex, que será feito na Bahia em fevereiro.

artigo.texto: David Sacks Warns the AI Data Center Pipeline Could Dry Up. Here’s What’s at Stake A permitting fight could stall the buildings that every AI chip, cable, and cooling system needs. While chip stocks sank in a single month, one corner of the market barely flinched. Which suppliers are exposed, and who collects rent either… This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them. David Sacks thinks the AI data center boom could run out of road within about two years. On the All-In podcast episode released November 7, which covered the midterm elections, the AI selloff, and what the hosts called a data center freeze, David Sacks said: “Nobody can make a $50 billion investment in conditions of uncertainty. I think by 2028 the pipeline will be closed or significantly reduced.” His argument rests on permitting. Sacks said the biggest danger is breaking ground and then, halfway through, getting “enjoined” or stopped by a worker strike or a community group. According to Sacks, governors in the largest data center states are “basically indicating that they favor a moratorium” until certain conditions are met. Why a Permitting Freeze Reaches Every Supplier A data center needs land, power, and a finished building before a single chip goes in. Broadcom’s chief executive made the same point on the company’s September call: “Before you get the chips out there, you have to get the data center shell in place and ready for production.” If the buildings stall, chip, networking, and cooling orders slow down after them. That dependency matters because each company in the chain is posting growth that assumes the expansion keeps going: - The company, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction), reported Data Center revenue of $89.02B, up 117%, guided next quarter to $108.0B +/- 2%, and disclosed supply obligations of $279.00B in its latest earnings release filed with the SEC. - Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) sees fiscal 2028 AI semiconductor revenue reaching $230 billion. That target falls inside Sacks’s 2028 window. - Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) grew revenue 58.5% and guided Q4 to $3.9B-$4.0B. It also disclosed that a limited number of large customers drive much of that revenue. - Vertiv (NYSE:VRT) reported organic orders up over 100%, and customers typically order 12 to 18 months ahead. The power, cooling, and networking names behind the data center buildings are a trade of their own, and we pulled together seven of them in a free report on the AI suppliers that aren’t chipmakers. Landlords Held Up While Chip Stocks Fell Over the month ending November 6, NVIDIA fell 21.4%, Broadcom 22%, Arista 20.86% and Vertiv 25.81%. Over the same month, Equinix (NASDAQ:EQIX) slipped only 1.85% and Digital Realty 3.47%. One explanation is that a freeze could help companies that already own permitted, powered sites. Equinix’s chief executive said, “If there are a number of projects canceled, then it only makes what is already scarce capacity much more of a scarce resource.” She added that across its 3 gigawatts of planned capacity, “the land, power and permitting are largely secured.” Digital Realty has 1.5 gigawatts under construction, 63% pre-leased, and a record $2.5 billion backlog that gives it visibility through 2027 and into 2028. Counterpoint: Permitting Outcomes Remain Unsettled Sacks’s view is a forecast. Proposed moratoriums can be narrowed, delayed, or dropped, and nobody knows yet how state policy will land. Vertiv’s chief executive called power, permitting, and labor pacing items that “are not slowing down growth.” NVIDIA expects fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70% and describes that outlook as limited by supply, with customer demand running higher. NVIDIA also cited top-five hyperscaler capex of nearly $800 billion in 2026 and $1.3 trillion in 2027. What Retirement Investors Should Watch Next Many people own this trade without picking a single stock. A major Nasdaq-100 index fund’s prospectus notes significant exposure to the information technology sector, so a slowdown in AI spending would show up in many 401(k) and IRA balances. Four signals stand out: - State action: whether moratorium talk in the big data center states turns into passed rules or remains at the proposal stage. - Guidance checks: NVIDIA’s results against its $108.0B guide, and Broadcom’s against expected Q4 AI revenue of $21.7B. - Vertiv orders: customers order 12 to 18 months ahead, so a slowdown in orders would be one of the first signs that 2028 projects are being pushed back. - REIT pre-leasing and pricing: rising rents at Equinix and Digital Realty would suggest that scarcity is helping the landlords even as new construction slows down. If permitting tightens, investors with heavy index exposure to AI hardware should know which parts of the chain depend on new construction and which ones collect rent on capacity that is already built. artigo.texto: - A 60 MW/600 MWh liquid air energy storage (LAES) plant in Golmud, Qinghai province, was synchronised to the grid on 30 October and has started producing power. - Developer China Green Development Investment Group (CGDG) says it is the largest grid-connected liquid air storage installation in the world, by both power rating and energy capacity. All major equipment was made in China, giving the project a localisation rate of 100%. The plant shows a route to long-duration storage that needs neither batteries nor underground caverns. The system uses ambient air as its working fluid. During off-peak hours, surplus electricity drives a three-stage centrifugal compressor that raises purified air to about 7 MPa. The heat of compression is captured and stored as hot water at up to 195°C. The air is then cooled in stages and liquefied at around minus 194°C, before being held in insulated cryogenic tanks at close to atmospheric pressure. When demand peaks, the liquid air is pressurised, heated and returned to a gaseous state, using both the stored compression heat and the cold storage media. The expanding gas drives turbines connected to generators. The cold released during vaporisation is retained for later charging cycles, forming a closed loop that stores off-peak power for peak use. Liquid air is about 750 times denser than ambient air and can be stored safely at atmospheric pressure. According to the developer, this addresses the relatively low energy density and weaker safety performance of some traditional storage options. Because the working medium is air, the plant produces no carbon dioxide or other pollutant emissions during operation. The equipment has a long service life and is not tied to any particular geography, allowing stable operation in extreme environments such as the Gobi Desert and high plateaus. The facility is designed to supply electricity continuously for 10 hours. CGDG estimates it can absorb about 600 MWh of surplus renewable electricity a day and deliver roughly 180 GWh a year, equal to the consumption of about 30,000 homes. The plant’s rotating machinery can also provide inertial support to the grid. It sits in Qinghai’s Qaidam Basin, a region rich in renewable resources, where long-duration storage could shift surplus solar and wind output to periods of higher demand. The plant was built by state-owned CGDG together with the Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). Construction began in July 2023. Hualu Engineering & Technology carried out the engineering design, and China National Chemical Engineering Third Construction took part in building the plant. The technology grew out of earlier CAS work that demonstrated liquid air storage at the 100 kW scale. To reach this scale, the joint team overcame bottlenecks in ultra-low-temperature cascade cold storage, developed an atmospheric-pressure low-temperature storage system, and solved the challenges of air storage and constant-pressure release. Domestically developed technologies include large centrifugal compressors, liquid expanders, cryogenic heat exchangers and integrated control systems. The project was selected for China’s national new-type energy storage demonstration programme and is listed among the National Energy Administration’s major first-of-a-kind energy technologies and equipment. Author: Bryan Groenendaal

artigo.texto: Insurance shortfalls, financial losses crippling St Bess business recovery Loading article... WESTERN BUREAU: Crippling financial losses, inadequate insurance coverage and mounting borrowing costs are threatening the survival of several businesses across St Elizabeth, leaving some operators contemplating permanent closure as they continue to reel from Hurricane Melissa’s devastating 2025 blow. Kadian Myers-Brown, president of the Black River chapter of the St Elizabeth Chamber of Commerce, and businessman Jason Henzell, chairman of the South Coast chapter of the Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association, believe that financial pressure continues to undermine recovery efforts. Myers-Brown said several long-standing, family-operated businesses in Black River remain shuttered because of the inability to finance repairs or replace equipment and stock destroyed during the hurricane, which struck as a Category 5 system just over a year ago. “Some persons are saying, ‘Hey, I’m just gonna give up.’ Some persons are saying that they are not going to reinvest ... not knowing what the plans truly are from the Government,” she told The Gleaner. Myers-Brown, an attorney-at-law, said some establishments had operated for generations without adequate financial reserves or insurance protection, leaving their owners particularly vulnerable to the hurricane’s devastating impact. “Some of them were like mom-and-pop stores operating for almost a century,” she said. A survey commissioned by the St Elizabeth Homecoming Foundation revealed that 46 per cent of Black River businesses suffered devastating or total destruction, with average rebuilding costs estimated at $17 million. Only 1.4 per cent had insurance coverage. It also found that 28 per cent of businesses reported income losses ranging from 70 to 100 per cent, with full recovery projected to take approximately 26 months. Among the establishments yet to recover are the popular Sunrise Bakery, several furniture stores, variety shops, barbershops, and farm supply businesses. Myers-Brown said supermarkets, pharmacies, hardware stores and medical offices were among businesses that had reopened, largely through the determination of their operators. Meanwhile, Henzell, who is also CEO of Jakes Hotel and chairman of the Treasure Beach Foundation, said tourism operators were receiving insurance settlements much lower than anticipated, creating additional financial difficulties. “If I were to take a survey of what people have told me in terms of the settlement that they got, it was probably two-thirds of what they were expecting. You know, it’s probably 65 per cent of what they were hoping for,” he said. Henzell further explained that lengthy delays in processing claims had forced some operators to borrow money. “If you have to go and borrow money now, because of the delay, remember you have to add that interest cost,” he said. He warned that dissatisfaction with insurance settlements was prompting some business owners without outstanding bank loans to reconsider renewing their policies, potentially leaving them exposed to future disasters. Henzell also stressed the importance of understanding insurance conditions, deductibles and underinsurance, suggesting educational workshops to help tourism operators make better financial decisions. “You could have the best hotel operationally, but you had the wrong mix of insurance,” he said, in highlighting the need for sound financial decisions. However, despite the setbacks, Henzell said all accommodation properties in Treasure Beach have reopened, noting that the recent Food, Rum and Reggae Festival generated strong occupancy across southwest St Elizabeth, extending into Junction. However, Myers-Brown said uncertainty surrounding the Government’s proposed Black River urban centre continued to discourage reinvestment, particularly among coastal operators, who are worried about what protection will be put in place to combat future hurricanes and storm surges. “It would not make sense to regain or restore business as per usual, not knowing what the effects of another storm will be like,” she said. “People are suffering. Businesses are suffering. Businesses want to really regain some sort of restoration at their peak level.” albert.ferguson@gleanerjm.com

artigo.texto: Maxell Begins Mass Production of All-Solid-State Battery Backup Modules for Industrial Equipment Power Supply Module Incorporating All-Solid-State Battery Helps Reduce Maintenance Workload and Improve Equipment Maintainability TOKYO–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Maxell, Ltd. (TOKYO: 6810) will begin mass production of its “All-Solid-State Battery Backup Module” incorporating the ceramic packaged all-solid-state battery, PSB401010H, and will start sales in Japan for industrial equipment applications in early November. Maxell has been conducting field tests*1 of power supply modules incorporating its all-solid-state batteries in manufacturing equipment at customers’ factories since 2024, with the aim of reducing the workload associated with battery replacement at production sites. The tests confirmed stable backup performance under actual manufacturing conditions, and customers highly valued the modules for their ability to improve equipment maintainability. Based on these results, Maxell developed four models of the All-Solid-State Battery Backup Module. The module is available with output voltages corresponding to those of ER batteries (3.6 V) and CR batteries (3.0 V), which are widely used as backup power sources. Two battery capacity options are available for each voltage type, offering a lineup of four models that can be selected according to the application. The all-solid-state battery incorporated into the module has an expected service life of more than 10 years*2. As a result, the module is expected to reduce the labor associated with primary battery replacement and the risk of downtime caused by unexpected battery depletion. In addition, the module can operate at temperatures of up to 85°C. Maxell will exhibit the module at Maintenance Munich 2026 (October 14-15, 2026; MOC – Event Center Messe München, Germany) and at other exhibitions in Japan. artigo.texto: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity Big Tech sees a culture war over progress. But the real fault line is electricity: drawing it from the grid and generating it onsite provoke different kinds of backlash, neither easily solved by public relations. This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape. Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words. But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity. Here’s why. There are two ways to power the sort of data center that AI companies want: connecting to the grid, or generating electricity onsite. In Virginia’s Loudoun County, where data centers are ubiquitous but have been built at a steadier pace than the breakneck expansion now underway elsewhere in the country, most are connected to the existing grid. One facility I went inside, operated by Equinix, has massive diesel generators onsite for backup but gets its power from the local utility, Dominion Energy. Much of Dominion’s electricity is generated by natural gas (which is cleaner than coal or oil, but worse than renewables). The average data center operating in this part of Virginia today has a power capacity of 54 megawatts. That’s more than the power draw of the Denver International Airport. Elena Schlossberg, a prominent activist against data centers in Virginia, told me she’s “always banging my head against the wall” when the industry paints the fight as a culture war. “It was always about power,” she says—that is, electricity. Some Virginia protesters appear more animated by a broader anti-tech populism than Schlossberg, to be fair. But it’s the particular consequences of drawing so much power from the grid that have done the most to shape how the backlash has played out. Recent protests have led to new rules from the state that data centers must pay fully for the cost of new transmission lines to the grid and make sure they’re not spread among everyone else. Data center developers told me they’re preparing for new rules that would cut them off from grid power during peak demand. Schlossberg also worries about the downstream effects of a strained grid—for example, that data centers will run more diesel generators or that Dominion Energy will expand fossil fuel inputs rather than renewables to meet demand. The overwhelming majority of AI data centers being built elsewhere in the country are not designed this way. The scale desired is so massive that companies are setting up in rural areas where there is virtually no grid infrastructure to connect to. Building there means bringing your own power (so-called “behind the meter” power), in the form of natural-gas-powered turbines. Companies also build diesel generators for backup. Anthropic, for example, has reportedly agreed to pay $3.4 billion for gas turbines in what’s described as the largest power generation purchase by an AI company. Even if grids were nearby, they’d be unlikely to serve the amount of power demanded. The smallest data centers attractive for AI training are 300 megawatts. It’s a lot of power for one industrial site, but not unprecedented: One data center developer told me he’s eyeing a former steel mill already equipped to draw that much electricity from the grid. But the ideal facilities are more like 6,000 megawatts. That’s the estimated draw of the city of Chicago, which is powered by more than 20 power plants within the city alone (and dozens farther out). The notion of data center companies’ bringing their own power might seem attractive at first, because they wouldn’t be straining the grid. But generating electricity at this scale inevitably affects surrounding communities, and when public utilities build infrastructure of this magnitude, communities have traditionally expected a say in where it goes. Now, private companies are undertaking projects on a similar scale. Natural-gas turbines of any scale release air pollutants. When diesel generators are used, it’s even worse. And in the unprecedented rush to get these facilities operating, companies have become horrible neighbors (recall that Elon Musk violated air quality laws when he set up dozens of turbines to power a data center in Memphis, according to the Environmental Protection Agency). Big Tech’s tendency to chalk the backlash up to a culture war obfuscates one simple fact: There’s only so pleasant you can make a small city of computers to live around. Sure, companies can pursue better deals that raise tax revenues, hire local workers, and get more community involvement, as the protests are leading them to do. But if a small town is asked to welcome a Walt Disney World, an international airport, a steel plant, and the power plants to run them all, should we be surprised by its trepidation? artigo.texto: Camila Valadão questiona licenciamento e impactos socioambientais A deputada estadual Camila Valadão (PSOL) apresentou uma indicação ao Governo do Estado, sob gestão de Ricardo Ferraço (MDB) solicitando a realização de consulta e audiência pública sobre a instalação de um data center voltado à inteligência artificial em Baixo Guandu, no Noroeste do Espírito Santo. A parlamentar protocolou um requerimento de informações sobre o licenciamento ambiental e os possíveis impactos socioambientais do empreendimento, além de questionar a participação da população e a disponibilidade de recursos hídricos. O empreendimento integra o Projeto Rubi, apresentado pela empresa capixaba Line Solution, e prevê investimento estimado em R$ 7,4 bilhões. Além do centro de processamento de dados, com capacidade inicial anunciada de 100 megawatts (MW), o complexo inclui condomínios logístico e industrial. A área total prevista é de aproximadamente 11 milhões de metros quadrados. A iniciativa da deputada ocorre em meio à falta de informações públicas sobre a origem da água que será utilizada pelo complexo e os procedimentos necessários para autorizar sua captação. Em resposta ao Século Diário, a Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA) informou que não possui registro de pedidos de outorga de direito de uso de recursos hídricos destinados especificamente a data centers. O órgão esclareceu, entretanto, que a competência para autorizar a utilização de águas subterrâneas é dos estados. Na indicação encaminhada à Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Seama), Camila solicita a realização de consulta pública, na modalidade de reunião participativa, e audiência pública para apresentação do empreendimento e dos estudos ambientais. A parlamentar também pede ampla divulgação das atividades para assegurar a participação dos moradores de Baixo Guandu. “Não podemos permitir que um projeto desse tamanho seja discutido apenas entre empresas e governo, sem ouvir quem vive no território. Estamos falando de um empreendimento que pode transformar a realidade de Baixo Guandu, com impactos sobre a água, o meio ambiente e a vida da população. É fundamental que as pessoas tenham acesso aos estudos, possam fazer perguntas e participar das decisões sobre o futuro da cidade”, afirma. O requerimento de informações foi encaminhado à Seama e ao Instituto Estadual de Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Iema). Entre os questionamentos estão a existência de estudos de impacto ambiental e outros documentos apresentados pelos responsáveis pelo projeto, além da disponibilização dos materiais para consulta pública. A disponibilidade hídrica é uma das principais questões levantadas sobre o empreendimento. Em reportagem publicada anteriormente pelo Século Diário, o prefeito de Baixo Guandu, Lastênio Cardoso (MDB), afirmou que a água necessária ao funcionamento do data center viria de uma represa no Rio Doce. Ele não soube informar se os estudos ambientais já haviam sido apresentados e direcionou as perguntas sobre essa etapa ao empresário Mário Rodrigues, fundador e CEO da Line Solution. Procurado novamente por Século Diário, Mário Rodrigues ficou de retornar à reportagem para prestar explicações sobre o projeto, mas não encaminhou informações até o fechamento da edição. Questionada agora sobre a existência de autorizações para o uso de água por empreendimentos desse tipo, a ANA respondeu: “Até o momento a Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico não tem registro de pedidos de outorga de direito de uso de recursos hídricos para a finalidade específica de data centers”. O órgão acrescentou que, caso o Projeto Rubi utilize águas subterrâneas, os pedidos de outorga devem ser apresentados à Agência Estadual de Recursos Hídricos (Agerh), uma vez que esse tipo de recurso é de domínio estadual, conforme a Constituição Federal. A distinção é importante porque a competência para autorizar a captação depende do manancial escolhido. O Rio Doce é um curso d’água de domínio da União, enquanto rios e demais corpos hídricos estaduais estão sujeitos à competência dos órgãos estaduais, por isso a definição da fonte de abastecimento é fundamental para identificar os procedimentos de autorização aplicáveis ao empreendimento. Em resposta ao Século Diário, a Agerh informou que não havia recebido pedidos de outorga de direito de uso de recursos hídricos ou de autorização da empresa responsável pelo Projeto Rubi e afirmou que, por essa razão, não dispunha de informações sobre eventual previsão de captação em mananciais da região para atender às necessidades do empreendimento. A preocupação com a água também foi levantada pelo coordenador do Observatório Capixaba da Água e do Meio Ambiente, Merci Fardin. Ao comentar o projeto em reportagem anterior, ele defendeu que os impactos sejam analisados de maneira conjunta, considerando os demais empreendimentos previstos para a região. Segundo o ambientalista, a instalação de novas estruturas industriais e logísticas pode ampliar a pressão sobre os recursos naturais e a infraestrutura local. Por isso, a avaliação não deve se restringir à disponibilidade de água nas proximidades do terreno destinado ao data center. A Line Solution informou à midia capixaba que pretende utilizar um sistema fechado de resfriamento, com reutilização contínua da água e reposição mensal estimada em volume equivalente ao consumo de três casas populares. A empresa também divulgou a previsão de criação de até 550 empregos, sendo 500 durante as obras e 50 na operação, além de arrecadação anual de R$ 50 milhões a R$ 60 milhões em Imposto Sobre Serviços (ISS). As projeções são da própria companhia e ainda dependem da implantação do complexo. Para além dos números anunciados, a definição da demanda hídrica efetiva, da fonte de abastecimento e das condições de disponibilidade dos recursos naturais permanece necessária para avaliar os efeitos do empreendimento sobre o território. artigo.texto: MIDDLETOWN, Calif. – The Middletown Area Town Hall, or MATH, will discuss data center protections and energy policy when it meets this week. MATH will meet from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 12, in the Middletown Community Meeting Room/Library at 21256 Washington St., Middletown. The meeting is open to the public. Viewers can participate via PEG TV at www.youtube.com/LakeCountyPegTV or on Zoom. Among MATH’s key items for the Tuesday meeting is the discussion of a proposed letter to the Board of Supervisors requesting consideration of adoption of a comprehensive Lake County Energy Policy. The letter also asks the supervisors to approve a resolution “to temporarily prevent new permits or land-use approvals for data centers, energy exploration, and similar developments from moving forward until appropriate energy policies and protections are fully established.” Once that resolution is in place, the letter said MATH has a “near future goal” of establishing a permanent zoning prohibition on data centers and all other similar developments within the MATH jurisdiction, which includes Anderson Springs, Callayomi Valley, Cobb, Cobb Mountain, Guenoc Valley, Hidden Valley Lake, Jerusalem Grade, Loch Lomond and Middletown. “We recognize the permanent zoning prohibition may be a lengthier process for approval and adopting the temporary resolution will provide the immediate needed protections for our community,” the letter notes. There also will be a report from District 1 Supervisor Helen Owen, an update from the advisory group to the Building and Planning Department, and an action item regarding discussion and a recommendation regarding personnel at Middletown High School. MATH – established by resolution of the Lake County Board of Supervisors on Dec. 12, 2006 – is a municipal advisory council serving the residents of Anderson Springs, Cobb, Coyote Valley (including Hidden Valley Lake), Long Valley and Middletown. artigo.texto: Foto da manchete: ilustração-Divulgação Por Jurandir Antonio – Voz: Enéas Jacobina Texto do áudio O governador Otaviano Pivetta está participando da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas, a COP 31, em Antália, na Turquia, com uma agenda voltada à abertura de oportunidades econômicas para Mato Grosso por meio da comercialização internacional de créditos de carbono e outros ativos ambientais. A missão acontece em um momento que o Governo do Estado busca estruturar instrumentos jurídicos e financeiros para transformar resultados de redução do desmatamento em receitas destinadas à conservação ambiental e à implementação de políticas de desenvolvimento sustentável. A COP 31 segue até 20 de novembro, reunindo representantes governamentais, instituições financeiras, empresas e organizações internacionais para discutir medidas relacionadas às mudanças climáticas, ao mercado de carbono e ao financiamento da preservação ambiental. Em Mato Grosso, uma das principais medidas relacionadas ao projeto é a proposta de criação da Companhia Mato-grossense de Ativos Ambientais S.A. O projeto de lei foi encaminhado pelo governador à Assembleia Legislativa e prevê a constituição de uma sociedade de economia mista destinada à estruturação, gestão e comercialização de créditos de carbono, créditos de biodiversidade e outros ativos ambientais gerados no território estadual. O Estado possui áreas dos biomas Amazônia, Cerrado e Pantanal, que apresentam características ambientais diferentes e exigem estratégias específicas de conservação. A programação da delegação também contempla discussões sobre riscos climáticos, prevenção e combate a incêndios florestais, economia florestal e estratégias para enfrentar crimes ambientais. Outro aspecto importante da conferência será a discussão sobre mecanismos capazes de ampliar o financiamento climático destinado a regiões que concentram grandes áreas de vegetação nativa. Pivetta permanecerá fora de Mato Grosso até 18 de novembro, de acordo com a programação divulgada pelo Governo do Estado. Sapicuá Rádio Agência, da redação em Cuiabá, Enéas Jacobina

artigo.texto: The 442 MWh Smareg 13 battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Vöhringen, Bavaria, Germany, is advancing through a partnership between ju:niz Energy and Envision Energy. Also known as Vöhringen II, the project will add large-scale electricity storage capacity to ju:niz Energy’s German portfolio and support grid flexibility as renewable energy generation expands. Announced on November 9, 2026, Smareg 13 will provide 442 MWh of energy storage capacity. The project will use Envision Energy’s Gen 8 battery storage platform. Additionally, it is designed for four-hour storage and will feature grid-forming capabilities to support grid stability. However, the announcement did not disclose its power output in MW, investment value or expected completion date. ju:niz Energy will oversee project development, financing and delivery. It will also manage the facility’s long-term operation. Meanwhile, Envision Energy will supply the battery storage technology and support project delivery. Smareg 13 is the third project under the companies’ partnership. Together, their portfolio will reach nearly 600 MWh. However, this figure represents the combined capacity of their projects, not Smareg 13 alone. Smareg 13 BESS: Project Scope and Technical Specifications The Smareg 13 BESS project will be built next to the existing Smareg 12 battery storage facility in Vöhringen. Additionally, this location will expand ju:niz Energy’s storage presence in the area. It will also strengthen the company’s collaboration with Envision Energy. However, Smareg 12 is already operational, while Smareg 13 remains a separate project under development. The installation will use Envision’s Gen 8 battery energy storage platform. It combines battery technology with grid-forming capabilities. Additionally, these controls can help stabilise grid voltage and frequency. However, their performance will depend on the system configuration and the requirements of the connected network. The four-hour storage design means the facility is intended to discharge energy over a longer period than a typical two-hour battery installation. However, the exact discharge rate, usable energy, efficiency and operating parameters for the project have not been disclosed yet. The Smareg 13 BESS project also features a low-noise design to address site acoustic requirements. Additionally, this is important for battery installations near existing developments and noise-sensitive areas. Cooling systems and other equipment can affect noise levels. However, specific noise limits and performance figures remain undisclosed. Development Status and Delivery Outlook Smareg 13 BESS project is currently at an advanced stage of development. Construction has also not started. The project’s commissioning date and cost have also not been disclosed yet. The project builds on a partnership involving two earlier battery storage developments. However, Envision stated that those projects had not yet completed delivery when Smareg 13 was announced. Consequently, the new development expands the companies’ project pipeline, while further delivery milestones remain to be confirmed. Contribution to Germany’s Energy Infrastructure Battery energy storage systems help balance electricity supply and demand. They charge when power is available and discharge when the grid needs additional electricity. Additionally, they support Germany’s growing use of wind and solar energy. These renewable sources vary with weather conditions and time of day. Smareg 13 aims to provide additional flexibility and grid-balancing capacity in Bavaria. However, its contribution will depend on construction completion, grid connection and operational performance. Furthermore, the project will support the wider expansion of grid-scale storage infrastructure. This is essential for managing changing electricity generation patterns and maintaining a reliable power supply. Other countries in Europe are also working to increase their battery storage portfolio. Some such as the UK are even repurposing former coal site for storage projects as it being done at the Fiddler’s Ferry BESS site in Warrington, England. For ju:niz Energy, the development adds to a business model covering project development, financing, construction and long-term operation. For Envision Energy, it extends the company’s battery technology deployment in Germany through a growing relationship with a local storage developer. However, the companies have not yet disclosed the full project schedule, financing structure or commercial operating arrangements. Smareg 13 BESS Project Fact Sheet Project name: Smareg 13 BESS (Vöhringen II) Location: Vöhringen, Bavaria, Germany Project developer: ju:niz Energy Battery technology supplier: Envision Energy Energy storage capacity: 442 MWh Storage duration: Four hours Battery platform: Envision Gen 8 BESS Grid capability: Grid-forming functionality Site context: Adjacent to the operational Smareg 12 BESS Project announcement: November 9, 2026 Development status: Announced. It’s in the advanced stage of development Primary purpose: Electricity storage, grid flexibility and renewable energy integration Smareg 13 BESS Project Principal Companies ju:niz Energy GmbH : Responsible for developing, financing and delivering Smareg 13, and for operating the battery storage system over the long term. Envision Energy : Supplier of the Gen 8 battery storage platform and technology and project delivery partner. SMAREG 13 GmbH & Co. KG : Registered project operating entity listed in Germany’s Market Master Data Register (Marktstammdatenregister)

artigo.texto: Reprodução Governador defendeu a remuneração de países desenvolvidos pela preservação da Amazônia e do Cerrado. ANA ADÉLIA JÁCOMO KARINE ARRUDA DO REPÓRTERMT O governador de Mato Grosso, Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos), afirmou que a empresa pública estadual voltada à gestão de ativos ambientais deve se consolidar como uma nova e importante fonte de receita para o Estado. A projeção de faturamento com a comercialização de créditos de carbono ocorreu antes da viagem do governador para a 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), que é entre os dias 9 a 20 de novembro de 2026 em Antália, Turquia. Segundo Pivetta, a estrutura para a exploração desse mercado já foi aprovada pela Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso (ALMT) e o Executivo estadual concluiu o inventário dos ativos disponíveis. >>> Receba as principais notícias de Mato Grosso em primeira mão. Clique aqui! "A empresa já foi criada, já mandamos a lei para a Assembleia. É uma empresa que vai depositar o estoque de ativos ambientais e crédito de carbono que o Estado tem. Nós já temos um inventário do que nós temos para vender para o mercado. Tudo leva a crer que o mundo, em algum momento, vai começar a remunerar os estados e países que emitem menos e sequestram mais", disse o governador. Pivetta destacou que a neutralidade de emissões projetada para Mato Grosso nos próximos anos garantirá margem para a captação de recursos financeiros globais em favor da população mato-grossense. "O nosso balanço de carbono tende a ser neutro ou negativo nos próximos 10 anos. Então nós vamos ter mais uma fonte de receita que pode ser destinada em benefício do nosso povo, vindo dessa nova ordem mundial, que é o balanço de carbono", explicou. O governador reconheceu que até o momento o Estado não recebeu recursos financeiros diretos oriundos desse modelo em fóruns internacionais anteriores, mas ressaltou que Mato Grosso estará pronto burocrática e institucionalmente para quando as negociações globais se concretizarem. "Até agora não teve, teve muita conversa. Talvez essa da Turquia seja mais uma, mas existe o interesse declarado dos países desenvolvidos, especialmente da Europa, em comprar crédito de carbono e remunerar a preservação na Amazônia. Nós vamos fazer a nossa parte. No momento em que esse mercado de carbono começar a rodar, nós vamos estar preparados com a empresa do Estado constituída, com toda a burocracia vencida e as certificações necessárias", concluiu Pivetta. 1 milhão de hectares de eucalipto Em setembro, o governador havia declarado que a medida faz parte de um planejamento estratégico para estabelecer um novo mercado no Estado, com foco especial na inclusão de pequenos produtores e em regiões que ainda carecem de desenvolvimento. Pivetta enfatizou o potencial do Estado na produção de biomassa e na transição para uma economia de baixa emissão. "Nós devemos editar o decreto de uso de biomassa e até 2035, nós temos que plantar um milhão de hectares de eucalipto", afirmou o governador à época. Além do plantio de eucalipto, o plano de mitigação ambiental e industrial engloba o setor sucroenergético e de grãos, além da captura de carbono proporcionada pelo cultivo do milho e citou inovações tecnológicas já em curso no Estado, como o processo pioneiro de injeção de carbono no subsolo realizado em Lucas do Rio Verde, que visa neutralizar as emissões geradas durante o processo de fermentação do cereal. artigo.texto: Avantus, a San Diego-based developer, owner, and operator of utility-scale solar and energy storage projects, has expanded its corporate credit facility to $1.28 billion in total commitments. The financing increases the company’s borrowing capacity as it advances a large development pipeline across California and the Desert Southwest. The expanded facility builds on a $1.05 billion credit arrangement completed in August 2026, increasing total commitments by approximately $230 million. Avantus will use the additional financial flexibility to support its strategy of developing, owning, and operating renewable energy infrastructure as an independent power producer. The company’s development pipeline totals approximately 24 gigawatts of system capacity, including 13 gigawatts of solar generation integrated with 44 gigawatt-hours of energy storage. These projects are intended to support growing electricity demand while increasing the availability of renewable power during periods when solar generation is limited. The credit facility expansion brings five additional lead arrangers into Avantus’ lending consortium. The new participants are Helaba, MUFG, NordLB, Santander, and Standard Chartered. They join existing lenders including SMBC, which serves as administrative agent, collateral agent, and lead arranger. Other financing participants include ING Capital, HSBC, KKR, Truist Securities, Bank Hapoalim, CIBC, KeyBanc Capital Markets, Mizuho, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets, and Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking. The larger lender group provides Avantus with additional banking relationships and financing capacity as it moves development projects toward construction and operation. Avantus’ business model focuses on owning and operating clean energy infrastructure rather than exclusively developing projects for eventual sale. This strategy requires access to capital for project development, construction activities, and long-term ownership. The company is backed by strategic investments from KKR and EIG, which support its expansion in utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure. Its portfolio is concentrated in California and the Desert Southwest, regions with substantial solar resources and growing requirements for electricity generation and energy storage. Avantus estimates that its planned solar and storage development pipeline could provide sufficient dispatchable power to serve more than 10 million Americans. The company expects energy storage to play an important role in balancing renewable generation with electricity demand throughout the day and night. The increased credit facility strengthens Avantus’ capital resources as it pursues development of its renewable energy portfolio and expands its independent power production operations. Support: KKR Capital Markets and EIG Capital Markets served as placement agents for the credit facility transaction. Kirkland & Ellis acted as legal counsel to Avantus, while Milbank represented the lenders. KEY QUOTE: “We’re proud to renew and broaden our relationships with leading project finance banks, which reflects confidence in both our ability to execute and our trajectory as an independent power producer. We look forward to building on these relationships as we advance our solar and storage portfolio and scale our operating platform.” Omar Karar, Executive Vice President Of Capital Markets And M&A At Avantus

artigo.texto: BYD mira Rolls-Royce com sedã elétrico de mais de 1.000 km de autonomia Apresentado em Abu Dhabi, o Yangwang Altior tem 5,60 metros, um motor por roda e bancos traseiros inspirados na primeira classe O grupo BYD foi a Abu Dhabi mostrar até onde pretende levar sua marca de ultraluxo. Apresentado no sábado (7), o Yangwang Altior é um sedã 100% elétrico de 5,60 metros que mira o território do Rolls-Royce Ghost e do Mercedes-Maybach Classe S. Carros que ficam a milhas de distância do Brasil. O Altior tem quatro motores, portas traseiras que abrem para trás e autonomia anunciada superior a 1.000 km no ciclo chinês CLTC. Mas o melhor lugar para entender o carro é no banco de trás, disse em reserva à coluna Wolfgang Josef Egger, chefe de design da BYD global. O sedã de ultra luxo tem quatro lugares na configuração apresentada, 3,50 metros de entre-eixos, o que significa um super espaço para as pernas. Atrás, os dois assentos reclinam, têm massagem e elevam os apoios para as pernas. Ao acionar o modo de relaxamento, as persianas se fecham e a luz da cabine baixa. O passageiro ainda pode rebater o banco dianteiro com um toque para abrir espaço. Se precisar voltar ao trabalho, há uma tela retrátil de 21,4 polegadas no teto para videoconferências. O som Dynaudio na ficha do automóvel tem 39 alto-falantes e o porta-malas leva 532 litros. Jade, seda e um motor por roda A dianteira quase vertical e as portas de abertura oposta remetem à escola britânica do luxo. O Rolls-Royce é assim. A assinatura chinesa aparece nos detalhes. A Yangwang diz ter buscado inspiração num ding, antigo recipiente cerimonial de bronze que também dá origem a Dingyao, nome do carro na China. Na cabine, que estava fechada para acesso, deu para ver o telão de ponta a ponta do painel, há jade amarelo de hetian polido à mão nas saídas de ar, bordado de seda de Suzhou, couro semi-anilina e tapetes de lã. É no acabamento que a marca procura dar ao sedã uma identidade própria diante dos europeus. Irretocável. A base técnica é a plataforma e⁴, com um motor elétrico por roda e controle independente de torque. Segundo a fabricante, o sistema ajusta a força em cada roda mais de 100 vezes por segundo. É daí que vem a capacidade de girar sobre o próprio eixo, uma manobra curiosa em um carro desse tamanho. A marca também anuncia flutuação de emergência como no SUV U8. No dia a dia, o recurso que mais interessa a quem vai atrás é a suspensão ativa DiSus, que lê o piso à frente e ajusta a resposta em tempo real para reduzir as oscilações da carroceria. É mordomia total. A bateria Blade de segunda geração responde pelo alcance divulgado no ciclo combinado CLTC, padrão de homologação chinês. O Altior também é compatível com o sistema de recarga rápida Flash Charging, cujos tempos para este modelo ainda serão divulgados. A Yangwang não tratou dos valores muito menos dos dados técnicos mas anunciou duas versões: a Executive e a Bespoke. A série limitada Shanhe Dingyun inaugura a linha personalizável com carroceria em tons de marrom e dourado que será exibida no próximo salão de Xangai entre 23 de abril e 2 de maio de 2027 no National Exhibition and Convention Center (NECC). E no Brasil? Como esta coluna antecipou, a Yangwang prepara sua chegada ao Brasil entre o final do primeiro e começo do segundo semestre de 2027, com o SUV U8 e o esportivo U9 entre os primeiros modelos previstos. "O Altior segue sem estreia comercial no país", disse, em Abu Dhabi, Tyler Li, presidente da montadora no país.

artigo.texto: Industrial Manufacturing Data Center Ballot Measures Pass by Wide Margins in Dozens of Communities In last week's elections, voters in small and rural communities adopted dozens of local proposals to pause, limit or ban construction of data centers. Released Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Written by John Egan for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary In last week's elections, voters in small and rural communities adopted dozens of local proposals to pause, limit or ban construction of data centers. Voters Turn Against Data Centers in Local Elections On November 3, voters in 40 local jurisdictions across 10 states turned decisively against data centers, voting to either pause, impede or ban them by 3-to-1 or 4-to-1 margins, according to data tracked by the ballot-tracking website Ballotpedia. The local results are best read as strong, place-specific NIMBY ("Not in My Backyard") resistance in communities where the issue was salient enough to reach the ballot, typically in smaller and rural communities. In a comparatively small handful of local communities, voters backed data center bans, moratoria, size limits or extra review requirements. But there were no state-wide or national data center measures on the November 3 ballot. Ohio alone had 21 data center measures, all of which went against data centers. In addition, seven Illinois communities also voted against data center measures. Small or rural communities in California, Florida, Kansas, Maine, Nevada, New Jersey and Wisconsin also voted against data center-related measures on Election Day, Ballotpedia said. Earlier this year, the vote-tracking website said voters opposed data center measures in six small communities in New Hampshire, Wisconsin, Michigan and California. Later this year, voters will decide the fate of data center initiatives in three small communities in Arkansas and North Dakota, Ballotpedia said. Only one of those local measures passed: In Harwood, North Dakota, voters rejected a proposal that would require additional review before the city could approve of future industrial developments, including data centers. Although data center measures appeared on ballots for federal, state and local offices, the results do not appear to signal a generalized, national turn against the data centers many see as key to dominating 21st century economic and national security strength. In an NBC voter exit poll, voters said four issues--government corruption, cost of living, the war in Iran and immigration enforcement--were the most important issues for them. Approximately 56% said artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress. By the Numbers - 41: Number of initiatives relating to data centers that went before the voters in small and rural communities in 10 states November 3. Voters in nearly all cases opposed data centers. - 6: Number of local initiatives in four states opposing or limiting data centers that were voted on before November 3. - 3: Number of voter initiatives relating to data centers in Arkansas and North Dakota that will be voted on in December. Data Centers Likely to Continue Moving Forward The scope and scale of U.S. data center construction plans is unprecedented. For more on that, see September 22, 2026, article - As Data Center Construction Plans Soar, U.S. Electric Utilities Race to Serve Once-in-a-Lifetime Load Growth. Despite votes against data centers in small and rural communities in a number of states, voters surveyed in a national exit poll from NBC, and a national pre-Election Day poll from Fox News, agreed that other issues, among them government corruption, high prices, the war in Iran and immigration enforcement, were far more important to voters across the country. That said, Big Tech companies and data center developers will have to work with a very different Congress and a number of new governors. On a national level, Democrats flipped at least seven seats in the U.S. Senate and at least 41 in the House of Representatives, with about two dozen races still undecided. But both houses will have Democratic majorities when the next congressional term begins in January. Although a few newly elected senators strongly oppose data centers, they will be the most junior members in that chamber when they take their oath of office in two months. Junior members of the U.S. Senate typically do not have the ability to push their measures through that body absent broad support from their party, or from the other party. Election Day also brought a new crop of Democratic governors to office, and some of them opposed data centers. Voters elected new governors in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, states where the previous executives had been enthusiastic supporters of data centers. Those three states accounted for about 173 gigawatts (GW) of data center capacity, roughly 39% of the data center pipeline, according to an analysis by Industrial Info Resources. That said, the outlook for data center construction is not black and white. For example, of the 173 GW of planned data center capacity in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, 14.2 GW already is under construction. And no state, aside from New York, has instituted a pause on data center construction. Will the newly elected governors of those three states follow through on their campaign promises to oppose data center construction? If so, executive orders won't be forthcoming until next January at the earliest. Legislation will take even longer. In either case, litigation may commence. In several states, voters cast their ballots for candidates vying to be members of the state public utility commission, which regulate utilities. Early indications are that several data center skeptics were elected. artigo.texto: BYD faz acordo com a TIM para conexão da frota e da fábrica no Brasil Com parceria, diferentes modelos da marca passarão a contar com chips virtuais (eSIM) da TIM, com conexão 4G em 100% das cidades brasileiras e 5G em 1,1 mil cidades A TIM fechou um contrato com a BYD para fornecer internet a toda a frota de veículos leves da montadora chinesa no Brasil, além do seu polo industrial. Com a parceria, os diferentes modelos da marca passarão a contar com chips virtuais (eSIM) da TIM, com conexão 4G em 100% das cidades brasileiras e 5G em 1,1 mil cidades onde a operadora oferece cobertura. A previsão é de que cerca de 200 mil veículos da montadora chinesa contem com essa conectividade embarcada nos próximos 24 meses. Assim, a BYD busca avançar no desenvolvimento de novas funcionalidades que envolvam serviços conectados. Com o crescimento de serviços como inteligência artificial e uso de funções como mapas e streaming a bordo, um carro já tem consumo de dados quase equiparável a de um plano básico pós-pago, tipo 'controle'. Do lado da TIM, o negócio representa uma expansão no setor automotivo, onde já oferece conexão para cerca de 630 mil veículos. A tele italiana possui uma parceria com a antiga FCA (Fiat Chrysler Automóveis) – hoje parte do grupo Stellantis – para fornecer conectividade 4G e eSIM em veículos das marcas Fiat, Jeep e Ram no Brasil. O contrato entre a TIM e a BYD envolve também a implantação de infraestrutura dedicada de redes 5G e 4G no complexo industrial da montadora em Camaçari, na Bahia. Essa é a maior fábrica de veículos eletrificados da América Latina, com 4,6 milhões de m². O projeto prevê a instalação de sete pontos de cobertura externa e 63 equipamentos distribuídos entre os galpões e as áreas operacionais, garantindo uma rede preparada para acompanhar o crescimento da produção e as demandas tecnológicas do complexo.

artigo.texto: Governo planeja investir R$ 46,3 milhões em plataforma de gerenciamento de dados em data centers O Ministério das Comunicações informou nesta segunda-feira (9) que o governo federal planeja investir R$ 46,3 milhões no desenvolvimento de uma plataforma de gerenciamento e distribuição de dados entre mini data centers no Brasil. Batizado de Prisma, o projeto utilizará inteligência artificial para identificar onde e como os dados devem ser processados, distribuindo automaticamente os recursos computacionais entre diferentes infraestruturas. Na prática, o Executivo espera que a tecnologia reduza gastos com energia e custos operacionais, acelere o acesso às informações e aumente a proteção de dados estratégicos. Os recursos serão administrados pela Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), e o projeto será executado pelo Centro Brasileiro de Inovação em Tecnologias da Informação e da Comunicação (CPQD). O prazo de execução é de 36 meses, a partir da celebração do convênio de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação entre a Finep e o CPQD. O ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Filho, afirmou que o projeto possibilitará maior autonomia e soberania no tratamento de dados no País. “Investir em tecnologia nacional é garantir que o Brasil tenha mais autonomia para proteger suas informações e desenvolver soluções para os desafios do futuro. Estamos fortalecendo a inovação brasileira e criando condições para uma infraestrutura digital mais moderna, segura e sustentável, reduzindo nossa dependência de tecnologias desenvolvidas no exterior”, afirmou em nota.

artigo.texto: Solidion Technology Reaffirms Commitment to Address Growing Energy Storage Needs of AI Data Centers Solidion’s patented anode technology and PEAK UPS design target the space, lifespan and cost demands of AI-scale infrastructure. DALLAS, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Solidion Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: STI) (“Solidion Technology” or “the Company”), an advanced battery technology solutions provider, today reaffirmed its commitment to address energy storage for artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure, centered on its PEAK Series uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system. As AI workloads increase the power density of data centers, operators face growing pressure on the systems that keep facilities running during grid disruptions. Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) batteries take up floor space that could otherwise hold AI servers and additional computing equipment, and they require periodic replacement. Solidion’s approach is built around its PEAK Series, a UPS battery system built for AI data centers using its proprietary 5500 silicon-carbon anode cell, designed for AI data center environments and well positioned to address these evolving requirements. The Company’s strategy focuses on three priorities: - Energy density and space efficiency: Based on Company testing, PEAK is designed to reduce UPS footprint by up to 30%, freeing floor space for servers. - Reliability and longevity: The 5500 cell is designed to last up to three times longer than conventional backup systems, reducing replacement cycles and maintenance. Solidion is focused on advancing technologies intended to support demanding data center operating environments. - Materials-level innovation: Solidion’s portfolio of +385 patents covering silicon anodes, graphene and next generation battery chemistries, together with its pilot production facility in Dayton, Ohio, gives the Company a U.S. based foundation for developing data center energy storage. Jaymes Winters, Chairman and CEO of Solidion, said, AI infrastructure represents a compelling market for advanced energy storage, “Our focus is on translating our technology into practical commercial solutions that address real customer demand. We are not betting on which chips win; we are focused on supplying something every data center needs.” Solidion intends to continue pursuing opportunities to apply its battery technologies directly to end users READ the latest Batteries News shaping the battery market Solidion Technology Reaffirms Commitment to Address Growing Energy Storage Needs of AI Data Centers, source

artigo.texto: NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) has invited online bids for the supply of battery containers and Grid-Forming Power Conversion Systems (PCS) for its 10 GW/40 GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) programme. The last date for submission of bids is December 8, 2026. The tender is being issued free of cost. Brief Scope of Work Under the scope of work, NGEL has specified that the bidder must supply lithium-ion (LFP)-based containerised battery systems integrated with Grid-Forming Power Conversion Systems (PCS). The total BESS capacity covered under the tender is 40.580 GWh, which will be developed across three blocks in different phases. Bidders are permitted to quote for any one, multiple or all blocks across the specified phases. Under Phase 1, the required capacities are 4.98 GWh, 6.600 GWh and 5.840 GWh. Phase 2 covers a capacity of 4.560 GWh, while Phase 3 comprises capacities of 5.800 GWh, 6.800 GWh and 6.000 GWh. The projects will be executed in phases, with the selected bidder responsible for supervising the erection, installation and commissioning of the systems at the respective project sites, up to the PCS output terminals. The bidder will also be responsible for servicing and maintaining the systems for 15 years from the commissioning date of each project under a Long-Term Service Agreement (LTSA).
